articles.titleTr: Analysts see no broader ‘contagion’ from $6.3B Binance hack
articles.summaryTr: Binance’s pledge to cover all user losses helped contain the fallout from the $6.3 billion hack, analysts said.
articles.articleText: Analysts see no broader ‘contagion’ from $6.3B Binance hack Binance’s pledge to cover all user losses helped contain the fallout from the $6.3 billion hack, analysts said. Binance’s pledge to cover user losses from its $6.3 billion hack helped contain the fallout across crypto markets, analysts told Cointelegraph. “There doesn’t seem to be any contagion-type effect from the hack, given that Binance is able to cover the losses using its balance sheet,” Martin Lee, market insights lead at DWF Labs, told Cointelegraph. He said investors turned their focus to the implications of the US midterm elections. Binance’s daily net outflows fell to $458 million in the 24 hours leading to Monday’s publication time, down from $6.1 billion on Nov. 2 after withdrawals resumed, according to DefiLlama. Attackers stole about $6.3 billion from Binance hot wallets in the Oct. 29 breach, making it the largest crypto hack to date. Bitcoin (BTC) fell as much as 5.7% over the first five days after the hack, a decline CryptoQuant called “modest” in its Wednesday report . Bitcoin fell roughly 13.6% after the $1.4 billion Bybit hack in 2025 and about 9.9% after the Coincheck hack in 2018. At least 14 of the past 38 hacks CryptoQuant reviewed were followed by steeper Bitcoin declines. Bitcoin’s drawdown after the Binance hack, compared to previous exchange hacks. Source: CryptoQuant Major exchange hacks have previously triggered “short-lived drawdowns that markets later absorbed” as long-term holder demand returned, Lacie Zhang, research lead at Bitget Wallet, told Cointelegraph, adding that the Binance hack does not represent a “structural trend reversal” for crypto markets. Related: Binance hackers had 8-week intrusion window before $6.3B exploit: SEAL Bitfinex analysts say CPI could help confirm a Bitcoin bottom “Much of the hack’s impact now looks priced in,” with Bitcoin currently trading at an “attractive level,” Bitfinex analysts told Cointelegraph. “Confirmation of a market bottom now depends on the Consumer Price Index (CPI) reading due on 10 November, which will shape the Federal Reserve’s next rate decision. Higher bond yields would put pressure on risk assets.” Market participants priced in an 80% chance that the Federal Reserve will raise rates at its Dec. 9 meeting, up from 69% a month earlier, according to the CMEGroup’s FedWatch tool. Bitcoin fell 2.5% over 24 hours to $74,580 as of 1:21 pm UTC on Monday, according to CoinMarketCap. Magazine: Vitalik ‘pivots’ ETH to store of value, crypto suffers after US midterms: Hodler’s Digest

articles.titleTr: Here’s what happened in crypto today
articles.summaryTr: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
articles.articleText: Here’s what happened in crypto today Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation. Today in crypto, the European Union called on the finance industry to write a common rulebook for tokenized securities, Zcash developers seek another reduction in block times and Binance France is closing up shop in the country. EU taps industry to set standards for tokenized securities The European Central Bank, European Commission and European Securities and Markets Authority are seeking nominations for an industry-led group that will draft common standards for holding and settling tokenized securities. Eligible applicants include EU industry associations, global institutions, private firms and fintech companies. They can apply to the European Tokenisation Standards Group (ETSG) by Nov. 27, with work set to begin in January 2027, according to a release published Monday. The three EU institutions will participate as observers. The group will develop technical and market standards to help companies hold and settle tokenized securities across different distributed ledger technology (DLT) platforms and ensure those platforms can work with existing financial systems. The group aims to produce an initial set of standards by early 2028, according to its mandate. The standards will support Appia, the Eurosystem’s initiative to develop a blueprint for Europe’s tokenized financial markets. The institutions warned that fragmentation could limit the benefits of tokenization and said the group may recommend ways for EU authorities to encourage firms to adopt its standards. In September, the Eurosystem launched Pontes, a system that allows financial institutions to settle wholesale transactions in tokenized assets in central bank money. Zcash devs propose another block time cut days after NU7 upgrade Zcash developers have proposed reducing the blockchain’s target block interval from 25 seconds to 20 seconds, seeking faster transaction confirmations days after activating the NU7 upgrade. On Sunday, developers ValarDragon and Evan Forbes submitted a draft Zcash Improvement Proposal (ZIP) on GitHub, saying that they want the change to be included in the next community poll and considered for the upcoming NU7.1 network upgrade. The reduction would shorten the expected wait for initial transaction confirmations. According to the proposal, this would improve the user experience for point-of-sale payments, exchange deposits and cross-chain swaps. The developers said the change would not increase the network’s overall daily capacity for private transactions. The proposal would also preserve Zcash’s existing issuance schedule, despite blocks being produced more frequently. The proposal comes just days after Zcash’s NU7 upgrade went live. On Friday, the NU7 upgrade was activated on the mainnet, cutting the network’s target block interval from 75 seconds to 25 seconds. The upgrade also introduced a Network Sustainability Mechanism designed to recycle a portion of transaction fees into future mining rewards while preserving Zcash’s 21 million ZEC supply cap. Binance France emails announce closure of accounts Dec. 31 Binance France is closing up shop in the country. Customers have been notified by email during early November, according to media reports. All accounts will be closed on Dec. 31, and any assets left on the exchange will be charged monthly fees starting on Nov. 29, Cryptoast, Crypto Briefing and other media reported on Saturday, citing emails sent to users by Binance. On that date, accounts still maintaining a balance will pay a monthly maintenance fee of 0.025% of the balance, or a minimum of 10 USDC, a stablecoin tracking the US dollar. To avoid fees, withdrawals must be completed by Nov. 29, the exchange said.

articles.title: The $2.85B Binance hackers lost shows why the UK needs stablecoin freeze rules
articles.summary: The Binance hack proved stablecoin freezes work. Now the UK should make clear freeze rules a condition of listing coins.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: The $2.85B Binance hackers lost shows why the UK needs stablecoin freeze rules
articles.summaryTr: The Binance hack proved stablecoin freezes work. Now the UK should make clear freeze rules a condition of listing coins.
articles.articleText: The $2.85B Binance hackers lost shows why the UK needs stablecoin freeze rules The Binance hack proved stablecoin freezes work. Now the UK should make clear freeze rules a condition of listing coins. Opinion by Lissele Pratt, co-founder, Capitalixe Last weekend, the Federal Bureau of Investigation claimed that North Korea was behind the $6.3 billion Binance hack, which analysts are calling the largest heist on record. While I’ve read a lot about the scale of this heist, far less has been said about what went right. Because while it is true that the perpetrators stole $6.3 billion, they haven’t actually been able to hold on to a significant proportion of those takings. $2.85 billion of the funds has been frozen. The reason for this comes down to what the stolen money was comprised of. Of that $2.85 billion, 94% was held in stablecoins. While this hack was terrible news all around, it did show that centralized control, oftentimes criticized by crypto purists, might actually be one of the strongest tools we have against crypto crime. Because, unlike other assets, stablecoins can be frozen by their issuers, giving victims a real chance to stop stolen money reaching the wrong hands. It does, however, raise an uncomfortable question. If private companies have the power to freeze billions of dollars in assets, who decides when they should be allowed to use it? The United Kingdom now has the opportunity to do just that. The race to get rid of stablecoins To get an idea of just how much the freeze mattered, you just have to look at what the hackers did within the first hour of their heist. Related: Binance, Polymarket seek Polygon hard fork to recover $6.8M in stolen crypto Clearly, they understood that there was a very limited window to move the stablecoins before anyone could stop them. So that’s exactly what they did. What was frozen from the Binance hack. Source: Elliptic Less than an hour after the hack began, they had already sold $325 million worth of stolen USDT (Tether’s stablecoin) for Ether. The reasoning behind this was to swap an asset that could be frozen with one that could not. Luckily, stablecoin issuers were quick to act, with Tether’s first major freeze coming just 37 minutes after the stolen funds reached the hackers’ main wallet, and Circle following three minutes later, blocking the movement of USDC. Without Tether and Circle intervening, far more of the funds could have ended up beyond their reach. We’re yet to agree on the rules The freeze, to its credit, worked for the most part because a handful of companies decided, in real time, to use it. The problem is that there still isn’t an agreed standard that outlines when a freeze is justified or how quickly the response needs to be, and we’re beginning to see the consequences of not having these answers. For instance, Circle is facing a proposed class action from Drift Protocol investors who allege it failed to freeze around $230 million in stolen USDC after the April hack. Their argument is that Circle could have stopped the money from moving, but didn’t act in time. Meanwhile, Tether is being sued in New York by two businessmen who claim it froze millions of their assets months before a seizure warrant existed. It’s important to mention that Tether has responded to this case, calling these allegations baseless. Working in payments and banking, it’s not uncommon for me to see traditional banks freeze money and accounts. Due to this, you may argue that if a bank can do this frequently, why shouldn’t a stablecoin issuer be able to? Stablecoin freeze timeline. Source: CertiK My argument isn’t that they shouldn’t. But banks don’t get to decide they want to freeze assets out of nowhere. There’s usually a legal trigger behind their decision, as well as a way to challenge it. Stablecoin issuers now hold the same power while having to act faster and across borders. So it’s about time they’re given some structure. Britain can fix this There is, however, a caveat with regulating stablecoin issuers. Tether and Circle, two of the largest issuers, aren’t based in the UK, so British regulators can’t simply tell them what to do. Related: Binance traces $6.3B hack to fake job interviews, compromised AI tool What Britain can control, though, is which stablecoins UK customers are allowed to buy, and they’ve already begun doing so. In June, the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) published its cryptoassets regime. Under it, UK trading platforms must carry out due diligence and publish a disclosure document before they list a coin, and that includes stablecoins issued overseas. It comes into force on 25 October 2027. The Bank of England is finalizing its Code of Practice for systemic stablecoin issuers by the end of this year. It covers stablecoins used widely enough for payments to matter to UK financial stability. Neither framework establishes the clear obligations around freezing stolen funds that I believe are necessary. But both are still taking shape, giving the UK the perfect opportunity to address this gap now, rather than trying to retrofit new requirements later. Two conditions for a UK listing So here’s a solution that I believe would work. Before a stablecoin can be sold on a UK platform, its issuer should have to agree to two conditions. The first being that it is contactable and ready to act. Tether and Circle did exactly that last week, but the victim was the world’s biggest exchange. A small UK platform should get the same response. I work with a number of smaller crypto businesses that don’t have Binance’s profile or a direct line to Tether. Under the current system, they’re the ones most likely to be left waiting. The second is that there needs to be a clear timetable for what happens next. If an issuer freezes funds, it should notify the National Crime Agency that same day. The freeze should then expire if there hasn’t been a court order put out to keep the wallet frozen. Neither of these are extremely controversial takes. They’d give law enforcement a chance to intervene when money is stolen and also protect people from having their assets frozen indefinitely, without legal grounds. The Binance hack has shown us that stablecoins can give victims of crypto crime a chance to stop stolen money before it’s gone for good. That shouldn’t be a privilege reserved only for the world’s biggest exchanges. Magazine: Can decentralized phone networks power the AI revolution?

articles.articleText: Strategy buys 1,036 Bitcoin as BTC holdings climb to 850,364 Strategy bought $81.9 million in Bitcoin last week while spending $188.3 million repurchasing STRC preferred shares, according to its latest SEC filing. Strategy bought 1,036 Bitcoin for $81.9 million last week, bringing its holdings to 850,364 BTC. The company paid an average of $79,012 per BTC last week, according to its Monday filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission. Strategy said it paid a total of $64.16 billion for its Bitcoin holdings, at an average price of $75,456 per coin. Its holdings now account for roughly 4.05% of Bitcoin’s maximum 21 million supply. Since the start of October, Strategy has spent about $1.06 billion buying back its STRC preferred shares, nearly five times the $219.7 million it spent on Bitcoin over the same period. Strategy spends $188.3 million on STRC buybacks Strategy raised $283.8 million in net proceeds last week by selling about $2.05 million shares of tis common stock (MSTR) through its at-the-market offering program. Strategy used $188.3 million of those proceeds to repurchase about 1.89 million STRC shares, following $208.2 million in buybacks the previous week. It spent $81.9 million on Bitcoin and allocated another $13.6 million to its USD Cash balance. Related: Strategy shareholders approve daily dividends for four preferred stocks Strategy’s separate US dollar reserve fell to $4.77 billion from $4.79 billion after the company drew $21.1 million to pay dividends on its preferred stock. Its USD Cash balance rose about 10% to $146.2 million from $132.7 million. The latest Bitcoin purchase follows Strategy’s acquisition of 811 BTC for $65.5 million the previous week. Strategy’s common stock fell 3% to $125 in Monday’s premarket trading, while its STRC preferred shares edged down 0.06% to $99.7, according to Yahoo Finance. articles.title: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation
articles.articleText: Release Number 9323-26 CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation November 05, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today issued an interpretation (“Interpretation”) of the requirement that designated contract markets (“DCMs”) provide competitive, open, fair, and impartial access to their members and persons with trading privileges under Commission Regulation 38.151(b) (“Impartial Access Requirements”). “Derivatives markets must operate on a uniform basis at a national scale in order to achieve the purposes set out in the Commodity Exchange Act,” said Chairman Michael S. Selig. “Geographic access restrictions are inconsistent with those purposes and the Act’s impartial access requirements.” DCMs must cease domestic geographic restrictions that violate the Impartial Access Requirements within 30 days, or else submit to the Division of Market Oversight (“Division”) an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. Further, within 30 days, DCMs should ensure that intermediaries accessing their markets are not impeding and are complying with the DCM’s Impartial Access Requirements, or else submit to the Division an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. The Commission will consider the facts and circumstances of any particular case in connection with potential Commission action. -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
articles.articleText: Release Number 9321-26 CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets November 04, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the U.S. Department of Agriculture today announced their signing of a Memorandum of Understanding intended to safeguard the integrity of U.S. agricultural markets. The MOU will allow the CFTC and USDA to harmonize policies and practices to better share information and increase access to risk management tools. The agreement will also assist both agencies with monitoring and identifying structural or potential systematic risks, among other things. “For decades, America’s agricultural community has relied on our markets to hedge risk, manage uncertainty, and plan for the future,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. “I’m proud that the CFTC and USDA have formalized this partnership through an MOU that will strengthen protections for America’s farmers, ranchers, and producers while expanding opportunities to manage risk through more efficient data sharing. I commend Secretary Rollins for her partnership and commitment to a more coordinated regulatory approach that safeguards the integrity of our markets and ensures they continue serving the agricultural community that feeds and clothes our nation.” “Faster and more transparent data sharing between USDA and CFTC is critical to helping our farmers and ranchers navigate an ever-changing market,” said USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins. “This MOU builds upon USDA’s ongoing data modernization efforts and allows our agencies to collaboratively identify risks and improve responses to market events. Breaking down barriers between government agencies to deliver for our customers is a hallmark of this administration and I am looking forward to the successes this MOU will bring.” -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
articles.articleText: Release Number 9320-26 CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas entered a default judgment against defendants Walter Dunning Larrick III and Cambridge Financial Advisors LLC for their participation in a commodities fraud scheme. In entering the default judgment, the court found the defendants fraudulently solicited and misappropriated more than $3 million from participants. The court found the defendants falsely represented they would use participant funds to trade futures and options, including those involving natural gas, oil, and gold; made material misrepresentations and omissions about the profitability of commodity trading with them; and issued false account statements to conceal their misconduct. The court further found the defendants misappropriated participant funds by making payments to existing participants in a manner akin to a Ponzi scheme, paying Larrick’s personal expenses, and sending funds to offshore accounts in Costa Rica. The court ordered the defendants to pay a $9,767,625 civil monetary penalty and $3,255,875 in restitution. It also permanently enjoined them from further violations of the Commodity Exchange Act and Commission regulations, as charged, and imposed permanent trading and registration bans. The default judgment resolves all claims in the CFTC’s 2023 complaint. [See CFTC Press Release No. 8768-23.] -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
articles.articleText: Release Number 9319-26 CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig today released a statement announcing that perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities can begin trading for the first time on designated contract markets that are dually registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission as notice-registered national securities exchanges to trade security futures products. Key excerpts from Chairman Selig’s statement: “Today, perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities (the ‘Equity Perps’) can begin trading for the first time on CFTC-registered exchanges. … “This expansion marks a significant step towards allowing U.S. market participants, consistent with applicable law, to avail themselves of the advantages of perpetual futures that have led to their emergence as widely sought tools for risk-management and price-discovery. I believe that bringing these types of innovative products into our regulated markets ensures that American investors and traders can access these products within the protections of the CFTC’s proven regulatory framework, rather than being forced to turn to offshore, and often unregulated, venues. … “The Equity Perps build on the foundation of the [Commodity Futures Modernization Act of 2000] and the [CFTC-SEC Memorandum of Understanding]. For too long, regulatory uncertainty left innovative products, such as security futures and equity perpetual futures, stranded in what SEC Chairman Paul S. Atkins has aptly described as a regulatory ‘no man’s land’ due to a lack of harmonization between the agencies. The CFTC and SEC have turned the page on that era, and are committed to delivering regulatory clarity for innovative products and a clear path to market, rather than more casualties of jurisdictional disputes.” Read Chairman Selig’s full statement here. -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
articles.articleText: Release Number 9318-26 CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading October 28, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced it will host an industry roundtable Dec. 15 to discuss issues related to the viability of derivatives markets moving to 24/7 trading. The dialogue will build upon the CFTC’s Request for Comment earlier this summer on 24/7 trading. The CFTC’s roundtable will provide a public venue for dialogue on the evolving market structures shaping derivatives markets, including overnight trading, tokenization, infrastructure and staffing needs, and operational readiness. Participants will convene from across the industry to discuss how the Commission can promote responsible innovation while protecting market participants and preserving the integrity and resilience of U.S. derivatives markets. “I have been consistently clear: under my leadership, the CFTC will not take a one‑size‑fits‑all approach to 24/7 trading. Market structure evolves best through thoughtful and responsible progress, and that’s exactly why we’re hosting a roundtable to hear directly from industry on their views for 24/7 trading across different asset classes,” Chairman Selig said. The roundtable will take place at CFTC’s headquarters in Washington. Information regarding the agenda, speakers, and registration will be posted at a later date. This event will be open to the public and livestreamed on CFTC.gov. Please note the number of in-person participants may be limited, and visitors will be subject to security checks. Members of the public are welcome to submit speaker nominations to [email protected]. -CFTC-

articles.title: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
articles.articleText: Release Number 9317-26 ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026 October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — Last week, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the Risk Management Center at Kansas State University co-hosted the 2026 Agricultural Commodity Futures Conference (AgCon) in Overland Park, Kansas. The two-day conference brought together industry leaders, policymakers, and market participants to examine critical issues facing the agricultural economy, developments in derivatives markets, and the risk management tools American farmers, ranchers, and agribusinesses depend on. Conference Highlights CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig joined K-State President Richard Linton to welcome participants on opening day. CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig addressed conference attendees, “I have spent a lot of time this year traveling around the country and talking to farmers and ranchers working hard each day to provide the food, feed, and fiber we depend on throughout our country and the world. I’ve met with farmers, ranchers, agribusinesses, and energy producers in Iowa, Texas, Nebraska, South Carolina, and Florida, and now, I’m with all of you here in Kansas.” [Watch Chairman Selig’s full remarks here.] Following Chairman Selig’s remarks, panelists examined the relationship between cash and derivatives markets, evolving commodity contracts, and the importance of effective hedging tools for agricultural producers. There were also panels where industry representatives addressed access to agricultural credit and the financial challenges facing producers and merchants. Additional afternoon discussions focused on rising production costs, fluctuating commodity prices, supply chain disruptions, and broader pressures on the farm economy. In addition, conference participants engaged in discussions about emerging market developments, including perpetual futures, 24/7 trading, and tokenized collateral, and their implications for agricultural risk management. CFTC Chief Advisor Alex Titus and White House Council of Economic Advisers Member Aaron Hedlund also examined the U.S. economic outlook, agricultural trade, and policies shaping American agriculture. The first day concluded with a keynote address from U.S. Department of Agriculture Deputy Secretary Stephen Vaden. U.S. Senator Roger Marshall of Kansas opened the second day with a morning keynote address on agricultural policy and legislative priorities facing American producers. The morning continued with discussions on agricultural prediction markets, the use of data in modern commodity markets, and developments in event contracts. In addition, panelists examined superintelligence, information advantages, and market integrity, including the implications of emerging technologies for market participants and regulators. Chairman Selig joined Futures Industry Association President and CEO Walt Lukken for a fireside chat examining the Commission’s priorities, the evolving regulatory landscape, and developments shaping derivatives markets. The conference concluded with discussions on enhancing public understanding of markets through data and customer education, followed by a panel examining clearing, market access, and the role of intermediaries in derivatives markets. Chairman Selig delivered closing remarks, concluding AgCon2026. -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report
articles.articleText: Release Number 9316-26 CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig announced the CFTC’s plan to increase the publication frequency of the Commitments of Traders Report (COT Report) from once to twice a week by the end of 2026. Data from Monday will be published on Wednesday, and data from Wednesday will be published on Friday. Both reports will be released at 3:30 p.m. ET on their respective publication days. Under the enhanced publication schedule, the reports’ latency will decrease from three days to two days. The change follows the Commission’s recent Request for Comment and reflects its commitment to providing market participants with more timely information about trading positions and activity in agricultural markets. The CFTC’s Division of Data is leading the effort to operationalize the expanded publication schedule through modernization and automation while maintaining accuracy. “COT Reports have been an important source of transparency for decades. Following feedback from the agricultural community, I’m pleased to announce the CFTC will be rolling out COT Reports twice a week to ensure this information stream is as useful as possible,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. -CFTC-

articles.titleTr: CFTC Sues to Block State Enforcement in Utah Amid Ongoing Efforts to Preserve Jurisdiction
articles.articleText: Release Number 9315-26 CFTC Sues to Block State Enforcement in Utah Amid Ongoing Efforts to Preserve Jurisdiction October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission announced today it has filed a lawsuit against Utah to block the state’s efforts to shut down CFTC-registered contract markets using state laws. The lawsuit follows Utah’s decision to file civil enforcement actions in state court against CFTC-regulated markets and other businesses. Utah’s effort to restrict the functioning of CFTC-registered exchanges obstructs Congress’s decision to federally preempt state law. “Utah seeks to shut down prediction markets across a wide variety of markets,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. “Event contracts do not just serve hedging and investment purposes—they also provide the public with information about the outcome of future events. Congress entrusted the CFTC to be the federal regulator with sole responsibility to oversee these markets. As I’ve said before, the CFTC has the expertise and responsibility to defend its exclusive jurisdiction over commodity derivatives, and that’s exactly what we’ll do.” This action reflects the CFTC’s firm commitment to maintaining its exclusive jurisdiction over CFTC-registered prediction markets. The CFTC continues to draw a clear line: if a state challenges the lawful operation of a derivatives exchange, the Commission will protect federal sovereign interests. The Commission has also initiated legal proceedings against nine other states and has submitted briefs in four federal courts of appeal and one state supreme court. -CFTC-

news.titleTr: TR Anadolu Metal'in (TRMET) 9 aylık kârı yüzde 39 geriledi! İşte 3. çeyrek bilançosu
news.summaryTr: TR Anadolu Metal, 2026'nın üçüncü çeyreğinde 778,9 milyon TL net kâr açıkladı. Şirketin çeyreklik kârı, iki kurumun 656,5 milyon TL'lik ortalama beklentisinin üzerinde gerçekleşti. Dokuz aylık net kâr ise yıllık yüzde 39 azaldı.
news.articleText: TR Anadolu Metal'in (TRMET) 9 aylık kârı yüzde 39 geriledi! İşte 3. çeyrek bilançosu - TR Anadolu Metal, 2026'nın üçüncü çeyreğinde 778,9 milyon TL net kâr açıkladı. Şirketin çeyreklik kârı, iki kurumun 656,5 milyon TL'lik ortalama beklentisinin üzerinde gerçekleşti. Dokuz aylık net kâr ise yıllık yüzde 39 azaldı. TR Anadolu Metal Madencilik İşletmeleri A.Ş. (TRMET), 2026 yılı üçüncü çeyrek finansal sonuçlarını 9 Kasım 2026 tarihinde Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu'nda (KAP) yayımladı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Şirket, yılın üçüncü çeyreğinde 778 milyon 872 bin TL net kâr elde etti. Matriks Haber tarafından düzenlenen bilanço anketine katılan iki kurumun ortalama net kâr beklentisi 656 milyon 500 bin TL seviyesindeydi. Böylece TRMET'in açıkladığı kâr, ortalama beklentiyi yaklaşık yüzde 19 aştı. 9 aylık net kâr yüzde 39 azaldı TR Anadolu Metal, 1 Ocak-30 Eylül 2026 döneminde toplam 2 milyar 15 milyon 127 bin TL net kâr açıkladı. Şirketin geçen yılın aynı dönemindeki net kârı 3 milyar 291 milyon 456 bin TL olmuştu. Böylece dokuz aylık net kâr yıllık bazda yüzde 39 geriledi. Şirketin satış gelirleri ise aynı dönemde yüzde 32 artarak 24 milyar 28 milyon 682 bin TL'ye yükseldi. Geçen yılın ilk dokuz ayında satışlar 18 milyar 166 milyon 341 bin TL seviyesindeydi. Esas faaliyet kârı 3 milyar 848 milyon 416 bin TL'den 6 milyar 526 milyon 427 bin TL'ye, FAVÖK ise 4 milyar 952 milyon 975 bin TL'den 9 milyar 916 milyon 118 bin TL'ye çıktı. Varlıklar ve borçlar yükseldi 30 Eylül 2026 itibarıyla şirketin toplam varlıkları 70 milyar 708 milyon 882 bin TL olarak kaydedildi. 2025 yıl sonunda toplam varlıklar 64 milyar 174 milyon 435 bin TL seviyesindeydi. Toplam borçlar 6 milyar 844 milyon 474 bin TL'den 12 milyar 169 milyon 506 bin TL'ye yükselirken, özkaynaklar 30 milyar 491 milyon 759 bin TL'den 30 milyar 827 milyon 467 bin TL'ye çıktı. Şirketin özkaynakları çeyreklik dönemde yüzde 3 azaldı. TRMET hisse çarpanları TR Anadolu Metal'in piyasa değeri 44,97 milyar TL olarak açıklanırken, fiyat/kazanç (F/K) oranı 39,12, piyasa değeri/defter değeri (PD/DD) oranı ise 1,46 seviyesinde bulunuyor.

news.articleText: Koç Holding, BİM, Pegasus, Doğuş Otomotiv... Borsada 140'ı aşkın şirketten bilanço yağmuru Borsa İstanbul'da 140'ı aşkın şirket, 2026 yılının 9 aylık finansal sonuçlarını açıkladı. Bilançolarda bazı şirketler kârını katlarken, bazıları zarara geçti. İşte şirketlerin geçen yılın aynı dönemiyle karşılaştırmalı kâr ve zarar rakamları... Borsa İstanbul'da işlem gören şirketler, 2026 yılının üçüncü çeyreğine ilişkin finansal sonuçlarını açıklamayı sürdürüyor. 9 Kasım Pazartesi günü çok sayıda şirketin Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu'na (KAP) bildirdiği bilançolarda hem güçlü kâr artışları hem de dikkat çeken zararlar öne çıktı. Bazı şirketler geçen yılın aynı dönemindeki zararlarını kâra dönüştürürken, bazı şirketlerin net kârında gerileme yaşandı. Özellikle sanayi, enerji, teknoloji, gayrimenkul ve holding sektörlerinde açıklanan finansal sonuçlar yatırımcıların gündeminde yer aldı. Şirketlerin 2026 yılının ilk dokuz ayına ilişkin net dönem kârları ve zararları, 2025 yılının aynı dönemiyle karşılaştırmalı olarak açıklandı. news.articleTextTr: Koç Holding, BİM, Pegasus, Doğuş Otomotiv... Borsada 140'ı aşkın şirketten bilanço yağmuru Borsa İstanbul'da 140'ı aşkın şirket, 2026 yılının 9 aylık finansal sonuçlarını açıkladı. Bilançolarda bazı şirketler kârını katlarken, bazıları zarara geçti. İşte şirketlerin geçen yılın aynı dönemiyle karşılaştırmalı kâr ve zarar rakamları... Borsa İstanbul'da işlem gören şirketler, 2026 yılının üçüncü çeyreğine ilişkin finansal sonuçlarını açıklamayı sürdürüyor. 9 Kasım Pazartesi günü çok sayıda şirketin Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu'na (KAP) bildirdiği bilançolarda hem güçlü kâr artışları hem de dikkat çeken zararlar öne çıktı. Bazı şirketler geçen yılın aynı dönemindeki zararlarını kâra dönüştürürken, bazı şirketlerin net kârında gerileme yaşandı. Özellikle sanayi, enerji, teknoloji, gayrimenkul ve holding sektörlerinde açıklanan finansal sonuçlar yatırımcıların gündeminde yer aldı. Şirketlerin 2026 yılının ilk dokuz ayına ilişkin net dönem kârları ve zararları, 2025 yılının aynı dönemiyle karşılaştırmalı olarak açıklandı. news.title: How a civil servant got away with juggling five jobs for so long
news.summary: Kashim Chowdhury has been convicted of fraud after pocketing £284,000 of taxpayers' money over three years.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: How a civil servant got away with juggling five jobs for so long
news.summaryTr: Kashim Chowdhury has been convicted of fraud after pocketing £284,000 of taxpayers' money over three years.
news.articleText: How a civil servant got away with juggling five jobs for so long - Published Aleesha Adams joined a video call with Kashim Chowdhury in May 2023. He'd been on sick leave from his job at the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) for nearly three months and Adams, his line manager, wanted to put a plan in action to ease him back into work. At the start of the call, Chowdhury was coughing and waving tissues up to the camera in an attempt to show how ill he was. But what really caught Adams' attention was how pale he looked. She noticed white powder had started separating from his forehead. "He was sweating, it was like rubbing off, so it was darker underneath and darker on the neck," she told his trial. She claimed he was wearing white make-up to look sick. Something he denied in court. Fraudulent behaviour went undetected Little did she know UKHSA was not Chowdhury's only employer. That month, he was also being paid to work full-time for the Department for the Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra), the Department for Business and Trade, the Food Standards Agency and the Home Office. He was contracted to work 183 hours a week – more than the number of hours in seven days. He fraudulently earned more than £284,000 of taxpayers' money. In total, he had eight overlapping full-time public-sector jobs between 2020 and 2023. During that time, this relatively junior civil servant was paid £350,000. Soon after her call with Chowdhury, Adams discovered that he had logged into the call using a Defra email address. When she challenged him about it, he blamed it on a technical error. She told the jury at his trial at Southwark Crown Court: "I believed he was lying." She escalated her concerns up the chain. But his fraudulent behaviour remained undetected. Chowdhury was able to keep working multiple government jobs until September 2023 when he left the Civil Service. He was finally caught in 2024 by the government's National Fraud Initiative, which conducts searches of Civil Service databases, such as payroll, every two years to look for anomalies. On Monday he was found guilty of nine counts of fraud and told by the judge that he would be facing a "very substantial custodial sentence". Chowdhury, 56, arrived each day at court alone. He is married, yet there never seemed to be any friends or family there to support him. He would often make his way down the corridors of the court building carrying two plastic carrier bags, with a bobble hat perched on his head. He sometimes looked bewildered in the witness box. Chowdhury, who had a diagnosis of PTSD in 2015, said that he had taken on so many roles because he feared losing his livelihood after experiencing insecure employment. He said he'd been forced out of a job at the Department for Education in 2013. He said he hadn't been thinking clearly when applying for jobs ''because of my stress, distress and trauma and due to my panic at the time". But the prosecution argued his behaviour was "deliberate" and "intentional dishonesty" and that he had exploited the system. However, the case raises important questions for the Civil Service. How was he able to get away with it for so long? Part of the explanation is that the Civil Service's human resources system is not centralised. Chowdhury did not declare on government application forms that he was already a civil servant, so the system did not spot the duplication. Hannah Keenan, who works at the Institute for Government, says the system clearly failed. "Government departments are taking hiring decisions independently of each other and without systems that join up," she said. "That the model and the culture surrounding it aren't working shouldn't be a surprise though - we've known for a long time about poor performers flying under the radar by shuffling between jobs." There are more than 550,000 people employed across the Civil Service, many in offices in Whitehall, in central London. They are responsible for carrying out government policy and the daily administration of the country. Another reason why Chowdhury's fraud went undetected is that he was working entirely from the east London house he shared with his mother. In 2023, she had dementia and terminal cancer, and he told his employers that he needed to be at home to look after her. But rather than reducing his workload to concentrate on her care, he took on more jobs. He covered up his impossible daily schedule by getting sick notes from his GP. In April 2023, he was off with what he called "mixed anxiety and depressive disorder" from Defra, the UKHSA, the Department for Business and Trade and the Food Standards Agency. While the sick notes were shown to the jury, they were not given evidence about what caused the depressive disorder or of a psychiatric assessment having been done during this period. His sickness did not prevent him from starting yet another job – this time at the Home Office. He did not mention to them he was ill, nor did he tell them he was working elsewhere. Unsurprisingly, a succession of his line managers told the jury he had not been very good at his jobs. Especially damning was the evidence given by Dan McCartney, who managed Chowdhury at Defra. He said he had to "effectively tell him what to do the whole time" and that Chowdhury kept his camera off during video calls for four months, claiming technical problems. But because Chowdhury was not subject to any formal performance measures at Defra, he was given a permanent job. He remained there for two years. In September 2023, Chowdhury was found to have more than £40,000 in his bank accounts as well as significant investments, including £45,000 in premium bonds. 'Risk averse' Civil Service A recent survey of 1,700 civil servants by the independent think tank Re:State found 76% of respondents thought it did not do a good job of tackling poor performers. An ex-senior civil servant told the BBC that much of the Civil Service is culturally averse to performance management. "Whitehall's known for ages it has to be less risk averse. Shrinking the Civil Service and the adoption of artificial intelligence technology make that more vital," they said. "But don't underestimate the fear factor: fear of drawn-out grievances and fear of being accused of wasting taxpayers' money if the Civil Service was to do what big private sector firms do, which is cut to get rid of poor performers by offering some money and a settlement agreement." A Defra spokesperson said: "Kashim Chowdhury abused the trust placed in him as a public servant and defrauded taxpayers out of almost £285,000. He will now rightly face the consequences for his actions. "This conviction is the result of a thorough and painstaking investigation led by the Defra Counter Fraud and Investigations team. It sends a clear message that fraud against the public purse will not be tolerated and those responsible will be held to account." The spokesperson said Defra would use "all available avenues to recover the proceeds of Chowdhury's offending on behalf of taxpayers". Chowdhury's case also illustrates a wider issue. He was engaged in what is being called "polygamous working", where people hold down several jobs secretly. Websites have even been set up offering people advice on how to keep their employers in the dark. Its rise has been blamed on larger numbers of people working from home. The government's National Fraud Initiative has identified 23 cases of "polygamous working" across London in its most recent report. It uncovered £500,000 of overpaid salaries over a period of a few months. Alongside the fraud case, Chowdhury is involved in a legal dispute with his three siblings, who accuse him of ''bullying'' their mother into signing over half of her £2.1m home to him in the final days of her life. He denies it. At times during his criminal trial, Chowdhury appeared confused by what he was hearing and blamed trauma for the web of lies he had spun. The jury took seven hours to reach their verdict and decided he was motivated by personal gain - stealing tens of thousands of pounds from the taxpayer. Chowdhury now faces a significant custodial sentence. Related topics - Published2 hours ago

news.articleText: Türk Altın'ın (TRALT) 3. çeyrek kârı beklentileri neredeyse ikiye katladı! İşte detaylar - Türk Altın İşletmeleri, 2026'nın üçüncü çeyreğinde 2,49 milyar TL net kâr açıkladı. Şirketin çeyreklik kârı, 8 aracı kurumun 1,30 milyar TL'lik ortalama beklentisini yüzde 91 aştı. Türk Altın İşletmeleri A.Ş. (TRALT), 2026 yılı üçüncü çeyrek finansal sonuçlarını Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu'nda (KAP) açıkladı. Eski unvanıyla Koza Altın İşletmeleri olarak bilinen şirket, yılın üçüncü çeyreğinde 2 milyar 490 milyon 253 bin TL net kâr elde etti. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Şirketin üçüncü çeyrek kârı, analist beklentilerinin oldukça üzerinde gerçekleşti. Matriks Haber tarafından düzenlenen bilanço anketine katılan 8 kurumun ortalama net kâr tahmini 1 milyar 303 milyon 200 bin TL, medyan beklentisi ise 1 milyar 254 milyon 400 bin TL seviyesindeydi. Böylece TRALT, ortalama beklentiyi yaklaşık yüzde 91 oranında aştı. 9 aylık net kâr yüzde 7 geriledi Türk Altın İşletmeleri, 1 Ocak-30 Eylül 2026 döneminde toplam 5 milyar 482 milyon 827 bin TL net kâr açıkladı. Şirketin geçen yılın aynı dönemindeki net kârı 5 milyar 922 milyon 218 bin TL olmuştu. Buna göre 9 aylık net kâr yıllık bazda yüzde 7 azaldı. Şirketin satış gelirleri ise aynı dönemde yüzde 35 artışla 23 milyar 432 milyon 408 bin TL'ye yükseldi. Geçen yılın ilk 9 ayında satışlar 17 milyar 325 milyon 5 bin TL seviyesindeydi. Esas faaliyet kârı 3 milyar 922 milyon 648 bin TL'den 6 milyar 745 milyon 92 bin TL'ye çıkarken, FAVÖK 4 milyar 849 milyon 977 bin TL'den 10 milyar 74 milyon 752 bin TL'ye yükseldi. Varlıklar ve borçlarda artış 30 Eylül 2026 itibarıyla şirketin toplam varlıkları 66 milyar 881 milyon 809 bin TL olarak kaydedildi. 2025 yıl sonundaki toplam varlıklar 59 milyar 481 milyon 939 bin TL seviyesindeydi. Toplam borçlar 6 milyar 319 milyon 398 bin TL'den 11 milyar 790 milyon 498 bin TL'ye yükselirken, özkaynaklar 53 milyar 162 milyon 541 bin TL'den 55 milyar 91 milyon 311 bin TL'ye çıktı. Şirketin özkaynakları çeyreklik dönemde yüzde 2 azaldı. TRALT hisse çarpanları Türk Altın İşletmeleri'nin bilanço verilerinin açıklandığı dönemdeki piyasa değeri 128,86 milyar TL olarak belirtildi. Şirketin fiyat/kazanç (F/K) oranı 27,64, piyasa değeri/defter değeri (PD/DD) oranı ise 2,34 seviyesinde bulunuyor.

Eski unvanıyla Koza Altın İşletmeleri olarak bilinen şirket, yılın üçüncü çeyreğinde 2 milyar 490 milyon 253 bin TL net kâr elde etti. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Şirketin üçüncü çeyrek kârı, analist beklentilerinin oldukça üzerinde gerçekleşti. Matriks Haber tarafından düzenlenen bilanço anketine katılan 8 kurumun ortalama net kâr tahmini 1 milyar 303 milyon 200 bin TL, medyan beklentisi ise 1 milyar 254 milyon 400 bin TL seviyesindeydi. Böylece TRALT, ortalama beklentiyi yaklaşık yüzde 91 oranında aştı. 9 aylık net kâr yüzde 7 geriledi Türk Altın İşletmeleri, 1 Ocak-30 Eylül 2026 döneminde toplam 5 milyar 482 milyon 827 bin TL net kâr açıkladı. Şirketin geçen yılın aynı dönemindeki net kârı 5 milyar 922 milyon 218 bin TL olmuştu. Buna göre 9 aylık net kâr yıllık bazda yüzde 7 azaldı. Şirketin satış gelirleri ise aynı dönemde yüzde 35 artışla 23 milyar 432 milyon 408 bin TL'ye yükseldi. Geçen yılın ilk 9 ayında satışlar 17 milyar 325 milyon 5 bin TL seviyesindeydi. Esas faaliyet kârı 3 milyar 922 milyon 648 bin TL'den 6 milyar 745 milyon 92 bin TL'ye çıkarken, FAVÖK 4 milyar 849 milyon 977 bin TL'den 10 milyar 74 milyon 752 bin TL'ye yükseldi. Varlıklar ve borçlarda artış 30 Eylül 2026 itibarıyla şirketin toplam varlıkları 66 milyar 881 milyon 809 bin TL olarak kaydedildi. 2025 yıl sonundaki toplam varlıklar 59 milyar 481 milyon 939 bin TL seviyesindeydi. Toplam borçlar 6 milyar 319 milyon 398 bin TL'den 11 milyar 790 milyon 498 bin TL'ye yükselirken, özkaynaklar 53 milyar 162 milyon 541 bin TL'den 55 milyar 91 milyon 311 bin TL'ye çıktı. Şirketin özkaynakları çeyreklik dönemde yüzde 2 azaldı. TRALT hisse çarpanları Türk Altın İşletmeleri'nin bilanço verilerinin açıklandığı dönemdeki piyasa değeri 128,86 milyar TL olarak belirtildi. Şirketin fiyat/kazanç (F/K) oranı 27,64, piyasa değeri/defter değeri (PD/DD) oranı ise 2,34 seviyesinde bulunuyor.

news.title: Republican congressman to force impeachment vote on Defence Secretary Hegseth
news.summary: The effort will likely fail, but Representative Thomas Massie wants to push Trump to fire Hegseth before Democrats can launch their own impeachment process.

news.titleTr: Republican congressman to force impeachment vote on Defence Secretary Hegseth
news.summaryTr: The effort will likely fail, but Representative Thomas Massie wants to push Trump to fire Hegseth before Democrats can launch their own impeachment process.
news.articleText: Republican congressman to force impeachment vote on Defence Secretary Hegseth - Published A Republican congressman plans to force a vote in the House of Representatives this week to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, alleging he has violated the US Constitution. "By engaging in hostilities in Iran for more than 90 days without congressional authorization, Secretary Hegseth is breaking the law and must be held accountable," Representative Thomas Massie said. The effort will likely fail, given Republicans will remain in power in Congress until January. But Massie says he wants to push President Donald Trump to fire Hegseth before Democrats can launch an impeachment process. Hegseth, who will hold a news conference on Tuesday about Massie's move, said he was not concerned. "We're not worried about that," Hegseth said when asked by reporters about the impending resolution on Monday, adding he would hold a news conference Tuesday morning "on that very topic". Hegseth's last news conference was in May. Massie, who lost re-election earlier this year, is among the few Republicans who have been critical of Trump and the war that started earlier in this year in Iran. The Kentucky congressman first introduced impeachment articles in September and is now pressing for a vote in the wake of Republicans losing control of both the House and Senate in last week's midterm elections. He has said his push to rid the administration of Hegseth is meant to prevent a Democrat spectacle next year. "My effort to impeach Secretary Hegseth is a much gentler version of what's coming when the Democrats assume control of the House and Senate next year," Massie also said in a statement. "They will hold hearings and trials." "President Trump should replace Secretary Hegseth now while he can still get a replacement confirmed in the Senate," he also said. Impeaching a cabinet secretary is very rare. The impeachment must be approved by both chambers for the secretary to be removed from office. The House has voted to impeach only two cabinet members in US history, but the Senate did not agree on either one. Once Massie introduces his resolution - expected later on Monday - Speaker of the House Mike Johnson must schedule a time to consider it within two days. Along with voting on the resolution directly, the House has the option to vote to refer it to committee or to set it aside. Massie will likely have the support of the Democrats in the House, with that party's leader, Hakeem Jeffries, saying on Sunday that he is a "hard yes" on impeachment. But Massie would still need to win over members of his own party. The House has passed a War Powers resolution - a measure that seeks to halt Trump from taking further military action in Iran - multiple times this year, with Massie's support. But Massie's disagreement with Hegseth also goes beyond Iran, he said in the statement. He has accused Hegseth of intimidating critics of the Trump administration, kidnapping foreign leaders and ignoring congressional war powers resolutions. Related topics - Published17 hours ago

news.titleTr: Dev kurumdan bitcoin analizi: Saldırılara rağmen piyasa direnç gösterdi
news.summaryTr: Binance'e yönelik 6,3 milyar dolarlık siber saldırının ardından Bitcoin'deki düşüş yüzde 6 ile sınırlı kaldı. Fitch Ratings, bu tabloyu kripto piyasasının daha dayanıklı hale geldiğine işaret eden bir gelişme olarak değerlendirdi.
news.articleText: Dev kurumdan bitcoin analizi: Saldırılara rağmen piyasa direnç gösterdi Binance'e yönelik 6,3 milyar dolarlık siber saldırının ardından Bitcoin'deki düşüş yüzde 6 ile sınırlı kaldı. Fitch Ratings, bu tabloyu kripto piyasasının daha dayanıklı hale geldiğine işaret eden bir gelişme olarak değerlendirdi. Binance'e 6,3 milyar dolarlık saldırı 29 Ekim'de başlayan siber saldırıda Binance'ten yaklaşık 6,3 milyar dolar değerinde dijital varlık çalındı. Olay, bugüne kadarki en büyük kripto para hırsızlıklarından biri olarak değerlendirildi. İşlemler geçici olarak durduruldu Saldırının ardından Binance, alım satım ve para çekme işlemlerini geçici olarak durdurdu. Para çekme hizmetleri 1 Kasım'da yeniden başlatıldı. Bitcoin'de düşüş yüzde 6'da kaldı Saldırıya ilişkin ilk haberlerin ardından Bitcoin, yaklaşık 10 saat içinde yüzde 6 değer kaybetti. Günlük işlem hacmi ise yüzde 67 arttı. Fitch Ratings, fiyat hareketinin geçmişte yaşanan büyük piyasa şoklarına kıyasla sınırlı kaldığına dikkat çekti. Fitch: Piyasa altyapısı daha dayanıklı hale geldi Fitch, kripto para alım satım piyasalarının daha derin ve çeşitlendirilmiş bir yapıya kavuşmasının bu sınırlı tepkinin nedenlerinden biri olduğunu değerlendirdi. Kurum, tek bir borsaya bağımlılığın azalmasının, belirli bir platformda yaşanan aksaklıklara rağmen piyasa likiditesini desteklediğini belirtti. Bitcoin destekli menkul kıymetler için görüş değişmedi Fitch, saldırının tek başına Bitcoin destekli menkul kıymetlere ilişkin analitik değerlendirmesini değiştirmediğini açıkladı. Kurum, daha sınırlı piyasa tepkisinin Bitcoin piyasasının likidite ve altyapı bakımından olgunlaştığına dair kanıtlara katkı sağlayabileceğini, ancak bunun fiyat, işlem hacmi ve piyasa derinliği analizleriyle desteklenmesi gerektiğini vurguladı.

news.title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy
news.summary: The share price dropped wiped hundreds of billions of dollars from the value of Nvidia.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy
news.summaryTr: The share price dropped wiped hundreds of billions of dollars from the value of Nvidia.
news.articleText: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy - Published Hundreds of billions of dollars have been wiped off the value of Nvidia after the US chipmaker announced an independent investigation would be carried out into its chief executive's affair with an alleged Chinese spy. The tech firm saw its shares fall by about 6% on Monday after Jensen Huang admitted having an extramarital affair. Nvidia's probe came after reports that the US believed the Nvidia boss had been targeted in an espionage campaign by China. However, China has rejected the claims, with its foreign ministry saying "allegations about Chinese spies were "entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China". Nvidia said it had no reason to believe the company's secrets or national security were compromised, but a statement by the firm's board of directors said it would begin an investigation in "light of recent reporting that founder and chief executive Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort". US intelligence officials believe Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, was a spy for Beijing, according to a New York Times report, external. The report said Secretary of State Marco Rubio sent a memo to top officials in Washington last spring warning that the Nvidia boss was in a close relationship with a Chinese spy. Alice Huang was managing director of Singaporean company Megaspeed, which has had dealings with Nvidia. Huang admitted he was "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting her and their children. He added he was "committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America's national security" and would cooperate with the investigation. After the investigation was announced, other big tech bosses, including Elon Musk, came out in support of Huang to continue leading the firm. US President Donald Trump said the Nvidia boss was an "honourable guy". However, the news sparked a sell-off in Nvidia's shares, with about $250bn (£190bn) wiped of the company's market value. While Nvidia shares fell, the US stock market opened on a positive note on Monday after last week's turmoil, with Nvidia's rival chipmakers benefiting. But analysts suggested the hit to the company would be short-lived. Victoria Fernandez, chief market strategist at Crossmark Global Investments said investors would not abandon Nvidia, because the chipmaker was so central to the AI industry. "Nvidia is the core of this AI trade, and without them, all these other pieces start to fall apart because the financing's not there," she told the BBC. Huang co-founded Nvidia, which is central to making the hardware for emerging AI technologies, with two other engineers in 1993. Its chips were initially designed for gaming, but Huang decided to turn its focus on AI development, turning it into the world's second most valuable company. Huang's position vulnerable unlike other tech bosses A key concern for investors going forward is what would happen to Nvidia if Huang was removed from the company, as Fernandez said there was "no natural successor" to the chief executive. Huang, unlike other founders in the tech industry, is vulnerable to any move by Nvidia's board of directors to oust him. He owns only around 3.5% of the company, and Nvidia operates on a single class voting structure, meaning his stake would not be enough to act as a veto power over any board decision. By contrast, many tech founders who lead their companies, including Mark Zuckerberg of Meta and Musk of Tesla and SpaceX, hold significant percentages of multiple types of stock in their companies. Fernandez said she does not believe the board will remove Huang as chief executive, unless there is glaring evidence of wrongdoing related to national security or intellectual property, "but I bet they start bringing someone up as his number two, to have there for the future." The modest fall in its shares mean investors believe it is unlikely he will step down or be removed as chief executive, but that the outcome of the investigation will be closely watched. Even people who do not directly own shares in Nvidia can be affected by rises and falls in its value. Pensions or savings invested in pots which have stakes in the company through index tracking funds can be impacted, for example. - What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy - Published3 hours ago Nvidia chips have been a major focus of the AI race between the US and China and the White House has previously imposed controls on where its advanced products can be sold. The H200, Nvidia's second most advanced semiconductor, had previously been restricted by Washington over concerns that it would give China's technology industry an edge over the US. But Huang has been against restricting the sale of Nvidia's chips to China, arguing that it would be better for the global rollout of AI to be powered by US technology. In January, the Trump administration said it would allow the company to sell its H200 chips to Chinese customers under certain conditions. Additional reporter by Samira Hussain, North America business correspondent.

news.summary: The outlet has been evicted from its offices of three decades and says it's been blocked from receiving donations.

news.titleTr: Russia's leading independent newspaper closes after eviction
news.summaryTr: The outlet has been evicted from its offices of three decades and says it's been blocked from receiving donations.
news.articleText: Russia's leading independent newspaper closes after eviction Russia's leading independent newspaper has closed after being evicted from its offices and facing pressure from authorities. For 30 years, Novaya Gazeta published investigations into corruption, human rights violations and abuse of power in the country. On Monday, the team behind the newspaper had a final editorial meeting before packing up their belongings and leaving. The Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Russia's media was highly diverse and that the newspaper's closure was part of "a standard rotational process". The BBC spoke to its co-founder Dmitry Muratov, a Nobel Peace Prize winner, about the closure.

news.articleText: Trump'tan ABD seçim sistemine tepki: “Bu sistemle seçim kazanmak imkansız” - ABD Başkanı Donald Trump, Kongre ara seçimlerinde kullanılan elektronik oy makinelerini ve erken oy verme sürecini eleştirdi. Trump, seçim sistemindeki mevcut koşullarda kazanmanın “imkânsız” olduğunu savundu. ABD Başkanı Donald Trump, Truth Social hesabından yaptığı paylaşımda ABD'deki seçim sistemini hedef aldı. Kongre ara seçimleri öncesinde elektronik oy makineleri ve erken oy kullanma süreçlerine yönelik eleştirilerini yineleyen Trump, seçimlerin güvenilirliğini sorguladı. news.summary: Eyewitnesses say the explosion shook the ground, with one believing an earthquake had hit near the Habas Demir Celik plant in Aliaga.

news.titleTr: Turkey steel factory blast kills at least 16 people
news.summaryTr: Eyewitnesses say the explosion shook the ground, with one believing an earthquake had hit near the Habas Demir Celik plant in Aliaga.
news.articleText: Turkey steel factory blast kills at least 16 people - Published At least 16 people have died and 13 others have been injured in an explosion at an iron and steel factory near the port city of Izmir in western Turkey. All those killed and injured were workers at the Habas plant, one of the country's leading steel producers, authorities said. Footage from the scene showed a large fire inside the facility and a towering column of smoke rising into the air. The local governor said the blast happened around midday after a crane carrying a replacement boiler collapsed, causing materials to fall into a furnace below. Workplace accidents remain a chronic problem in Turkey, the Turkish Health and Safety Labor Watch, an independent civil society organisation, said. Eyewitnesses said the explosion shook the ground, with one person initially believing an earthquake had struck. In a statement, the company said the accident occurred during scheduled maintenance work on one of the plant's electric arc furnaces. Izmir Governor Süleyman Elban told media that some people are believed to be still under the rubble. Speaking after a cabinet meeting on Monday, Turkey's President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan confirmed the deaths and said investigations were under way, while search and rescue operations continued. He also said two of the injured were in a serious condition. At least five people have been arrested, according BBC News's Turkish service, citing local media reports. The Habas plant is in the Izmir district of Aliaga which is a major port and one of Turkey's main shipbreaking hubs. - Published29 October - Published15 October

(CWENE), 2026 yılı üçüncü çeyrek finansal sonuçlarını 9 Kasım'da Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu'nda (KAP) yayımladı. news.summary: The pilot lets eligible corporate and institutional clients accept USDC on Ethereum, with each token converted to one US dollar before deposit.

news.titleTr: PNC Bank tests turning USDC payments into dollar deposits
news.summaryTr: The pilot lets eligible corporate and institutional clients accept USDC on Ethereum, with each token converted to one US dollar before deposit.
news.articleText: PNC Bank tests turning USDC payments into dollar deposits The pilot lets eligible corporate and institutional clients accept USDC on Ethereum, with each token converted to one US dollar before deposit. PNC Bank, the eighth-largest US bank by assets, launched a limited pilot enabling eligible corporate and institutional clients to receive USDC payments through Coinbase. The pilot accepts USDC, a US dollar-backed stablecoin issued by Circle, on Ethereum using Coinbase Payments products. Payments are automatically converted into dollars and deposited into designated PNC accounts, allowing businesses to accept stablecoins without holding them. PNC said the service aims to speed up access to funds and improve cross-border payment efficiency. The bank did not disclose fees, settlement-time benchmarks or the number of participating clients, nor did it respond to Cointelegraph’s request for additional details by publication time. The pilot builds on a partnership established in July 2025, when PNC agreed to offer cryptocurrency services through Coinbase’s infrastructure while providing banking services to the exchange. The partnership led to the launch of Bitcoin (BTC) trading for eligible PNC Private Bank clients in December. PNC’s move follows a similar initiative by Citi, which expanded its Coinbase partnership in September to enable institutional clients to accept stablecoin payments through its Spring by Citi platform, with Coinbase converting the payments into fiat currency. USDC is the second-largest stablecoin by market capitalization, at $70.5 billion, behind Tether’s USDT at $176.8 billion, according to DefiLlama data. PNC Bank, the eighth-largest US bank by assets, launched a limited pilot enabling eligible corporate and institutional clients to receive USDC payments through Coinbase. The pilot accepts USDC, a US dollar-backed stablecoin issued by Circle, on Ethereum using Coinbase Payments products. Payments are automatically converted into dollars and deposited into designated PNC accounts, allowing businesses to accept stablecoins without holding them. PNC said the service aims to speed up access to funds and improve cross-border payment efficiency. The bank did not disclose fees, settlement-time benchmarks or the number of participating clients, nor did it respond to Cointelegraph’s request for additional details by publication time. The pilot builds on a partnership established in July 2025, when PNC agreed to offer cryptocurrency services through Coinbase’s infrastructure while providing banking services to the exchange. The partnership led to the launch of Bitcoin (BTC) trading for eligible PNC Private Bank clients in December. PNC’s move follows a similar initiative by Citi, which expanded its Coinbase partnership in September to enable institutional clients to accept stablecoin payments through its Spring by Citi platform, with Coinbase converting the payments into fiat currency. news.titleTr: Trump questions midterm elections integrity after previously accepting results
news.summaryTr: Trump made the claims, without evidence, on Truth Social on Monday.
news.articleText: Trump questions midterm elections integrity after previously accepting results - Published US President Donald Trump has questioned the legitimacy of the midterm election results in which Republicans suffered sweeping losses, days after saying he would accept the outcome. "Does anybody really believe that this 'Election' was honest. How could the Polls be so wrong?" Trump wrote on Truth Social on Monday. This appeared to contradict what he told the New York Times on election night that he was "absolutely willing" to accept the results. Democrats retook both chambers of Congress in last week's elections. State and local officials across the US said voting had been mostly problem-free. Some key races, including Senate contests in Alaska and Mississippi, have yet to be called. In the Truth Social post, Trump made vague claims about polling, voting "dumps", and "machines" without providing specific evidence of what this referred to and whether he believed there had been error or wrongdoing. The reporting of vote counts on election night proceeded as normal, according to Charles Stewart III, a political scientist at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT). "We saw across the nation the standard patterns we see in terms of when the votes are reported," he said. Stewart added that in some states, like Florida and Georgia, some initial reporting of results happens quickly because they already have the results of early and mail ballots. Trump has previously attempted to cast doubts on the integrity of elections he has lost, although he himself was not on the ballot in the midterms. "We would have won easily if I was on the ballot," Trump told CBS News, the BBC's US partner, after it was confirmed his party had lost both the Senate and the House. Surveys ahead of the election from several pollsters and news outlets suggested that Republicans could lose seats in both the House and Senate. As it stands, Democrats have won 54 US Senate seats and 254 US House seats in the midterms, giving them comfortable majorities in both chambers of Congress even as counting continues in some races, like in Alaska and Mississippi. "State laws and practicalities are such that some states will just take longer to count," said Ruth Greenwood, director of the Election Law Clinic at Harvard Law School. "That doesn't mean anything nefarious is occurring—we just need to trust local election officials to count every vote and tell us the results when they are done." The outcome has been clear since election night. Trump told the New York Times then: "We'll, you know, look forward to working with [Democrats]", adding: "We'll probably work something out." He has also offered his own analysis of why Republicans lost, acknowledging on Fox News that the Iran war had contributed to the defeat. "People agree with what I'm doing on Iran but they really probably weren't willing to do the short term consequences of paying more for gasoline - I understand that," he said. Vice-President JD Vance has also blamed the Iran war, which began in February and which has severely disrupted global oil and gas supplies - causing costs to soar, as the reason their party lost the election. In the run-up to the midterms, Trump made claims about widespread voting fraud, despite evidence that it is rare. He and his allies alleged for months that the 2020 presidential election, which he lost to former President Joe Biden, had been rigged against him. His lawyers and allies spent weeks attempting to litigate the results, but courts repeatedly struck them down. The justice department during his administration has made unprecedented attempts to exert more federal control over elections - a power the Constitution primarily delegates to individual states. Days before these midterms, it filed controversial lawsuits in federal courts challenging the count and certification of votes in states like California and Alaska, but judges ruled against them in nearly all instances. Election law experts, state officials, and local elections offices told the BBC they had spent months preparing for a scenario in which the White House or election sceptics questioned the votes' legitimacy. Despite the intense focus around election integrity on both sides of the debate, top state and local election officials have reported a mostly smooth process so far for the 2026 midterms. Extreme weather did force some location closures, and a handful of reported administrative or technical issues slowed the process in some local jurisdictions.

news.summary: Avalanche’s AVAX token rose as much as 10% after the NYSE selected its blockchain to support settlement on a planned tokenized stock trading platform.

news.titleTr: Avalanche’s AVAX leads crypto gains following NYSE tokenization deal
news.summaryTr: Avalanche’s AVAX token rose as much as 10% after the NYSE selected its blockchain to support settlement on a planned tokenized stock trading platform.
news.articleText: Avalanche’s AVAX leads crypto gains following NYSE tokenization deal Avalanche’s AVAX token rose as much as 10% after the NYSE selected its blockchain to support settlement on a planned tokenized stock trading platform. Avalanche’s AVAX token jumped as much as 10% on Monday, making it the top earner among the 100 largest cryptocurrencies by market capitalization, as the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) announced plans to use its blockchain to settle trades on a new platform for trading tokenized stocks around the clock. AVAX later eased to $8.86, still up over 8% on the day, according to CoinGecko data as of 03:22 p.m. UTC. The token currently has a market cap of around $3.95 billion, with $439.7 million traded over the past day. The Avalanche blockchain boasts a total value locked (TVL) of $633 million, up 4% over the past 24 hours, according to DeFiLlama. “At the NYSE, we’re looking at how blockchain technology can expand what we offer in equities, and we’re picking the right technology for each job,” Dennis Lee, the head of digital issuance at NYSE, said in an announcement. The deal underscores a growing effort by Wall Street firms to use blockchain technology to make stock trading faster and allow investors to trade outside regular market hours. Typically, traditional US stock markets are open from 9:30 am to 4:00 pm EST on weekdays, with trades often taking at least one business day to settle. The NYSE first announced plans for the platform in January. In September, Ava Labs revealed that the exchange had spent about a year testing Avalanche, but the blockchain’s final pick was not confirmed until Monday. Related: Aave launches V4 on Avalanche, laying groundwork for tokenized credit markets NYSE chooses Avalanche Ava Labs said that the NYSE will use Avalanche’s blockchain to keep track of stock trades and help complete transactions on its planned trading platform. The platform will let investors buy and sell digital versions of stocks on different blockchains, while Avalanche will be used to record those trades and make sure transactions are completed. “The upcoming digital trading platform will support equities listed on a range of blockchains, though the ledger that records and settles trades needs to be fast and reliable, let us control who can take part, keep costs predictable, and have a large community of developers behind it. Avalanche meets all those needs,” Lee said. The platform could launch before the end of 2026 if it receives regulatory approval, according to The Wall Street Journal. “Our first conversations with the NYSE team began nearly a year ago, and it’s remarkable how quickly we’ve progressed toward supporting this infrastructure,” John Nahas, chief business officer at Ava Labs told Cointelegraph. “It’s an important step toward blockchain becoming foundational financial infrastructure.” Wall Street dives into tokenized stocks The news comes as other major financial firms are also investing in blockchain technology to make stock trading faster and available around the clock. In September, Nasdaq announced plans to invest $100 million in Kraken’s parent company, Payward, to launch tokenized stocks. The expected launch for that project is the second quarter of 2027. Meanwhile, the Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC), which helps settle US securities trades, launched a service in October that allows financial firms to turn traditional securities into digital tokens. “Today marks the culmination of years of work to bring tokenized securities into a regulated framework supported by trusted market infrastructure,” Frank La Salla, CEO of DTCC, said at the time. “By extending DTC’s resiliency, governance and operational standards into digital markets, we are establishing the foundation for responsible institutional adoption at scale.” The NYSE deal also follows other financial firms’ efforts to bring traditional financial assets specifically onto Avalanche. In July, Japanese financial technology company Progmat announced it had moved more than 452 billion yen worth of digital securities onto a dedicated Avalanche blockchain. And in September, Aave Labs announced plans to launch a lending service on Avalanche that would let financial firms borrow Tether’s USAT stablecoin using tokenized assets as collateral. news.title: Civil servant who secretly held five jobs found guilty of fraud
news.summary: Kashim Chowdhury had secretly held multiple public sector jobs on full-time salaries.
