items.titleTr: How a civil servant got away with juggling five jobs for so long
items.summaryTr: Kashim Chowdhury has been convicted of fraud after pocketing £284,000 of taxpayers' money over three years.
items.articleText: How a civil servant got away with juggling five jobs for so long - Published Aleesha Adams joined a video call with Kashim Chowdhury in May 2023. He'd been on sick leave from his job at the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) for nearly three months and Adams, his line manager, wanted to put a plan in action to ease him back into work. At the start of the call, Chowdhury was coughing and waving tissues up to the camera in an attempt to show how ill he was. But what really caught Adams' attention was how pale he looked. She noticed white powder had started separating from his forehead. "He was sweating, it was like rubbing off, so it was darker underneath and darker on the neck," she told his trial. She claimed he was wearing white make-up to look sick. Something he denied in court. Fraudulent behaviour went undetected Little did she know UKHSA was not Chowdhury's only employer. That month, he was also being paid to work full-time for the Department for the Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra), the Department for Business and Trade, the Food Standards Agency and the Home Office. He was contracted to work 183 hours a week – more than the number of hours in seven days. He fraudulently earned more than £284,000 of taxpayers' money. In total, he had eight overlapping full-time public-sector jobs between 2020 and 2023. During that time, this relatively junior civil servant was paid £350,000. Soon after her call with Chowdhury, Adams discovered that he had logged into the call using a Defra email address. When she challenged him about it, he blamed it on a technical error. She told the jury at his trial at Southwark Crown Court: "I believed he was lying." She escalated her concerns up the chain. But his fraudulent behaviour remained undetected. Chowdhury was able to keep working multiple government jobs until September 2023 when he left the Civil Service. He was finally caught in 2024 by the government's National Fraud Initiative, which conducts searches of Civil Service databases, such as payroll, every two years to look for anomalies. On Monday he was found guilty of nine counts of fraud and told by the judge that he would be facing a "very substantial custodial sentence". Chowdhury, 56, arrived each day at court alone. He is married, yet there never seemed to be any friends or family there to support him. He would often make his way down the corridors of the court building carrying two plastic carrier bags, with a bobble hat perched on his head. He sometimes looked bewildered in the witness box. Chowdhury, who had a diagnosis of PTSD in 2015, said that he had taken on so many roles because he feared losing his livelihood after experiencing insecure employment. He said he'd been forced out of a job at the Department for Education in 2013. He said he hadn't been thinking clearly when applying for jobs ''because of my stress, distress and trauma and due to my panic at the time". But the prosecution argued his behaviour was "deliberate" and "intentional dishonesty" and that he had exploited the system. However, the case raises important questions for the Civil Service. How was he able to get away with it for so long? Part of the explanation is that the Civil Service's human resources system is not centralised. Chowdhury did not declare on government application forms that he was already a civil servant, so the system did not spot the duplication. Hannah Keenan, who works at the Institute for Government, says the system clearly failed. "Government departments are taking hiring decisions independently of each other and without systems that join up," she said. "That the model and the culture surrounding it aren't working shouldn't be a surprise though - we've known for a long time about poor performers flying under the radar by shuffling between jobs." There are more than 550,000 people employed across the Civil Service, many in offices in Whitehall, in central London. They are responsible for carrying out government policy and the daily administration of the country. Another reason why Chowdhury's fraud went undetected is that he was working entirely from the east London house he shared with his mother. In 2023, she had dementia and terminal cancer, and he told his employers that he needed to be at home to look after her. But rather than reducing his workload to concentrate on her care, he took on more jobs. He covered up his impossible daily schedule by getting sick notes from his GP. In April 2023, he was off with what he called "mixed anxiety and depressive disorder" from Defra, the UKHSA, the Department for Business and Trade and the Food Standards Agency. While the sick notes were shown to the jury, they were not given evidence about what caused the depressive disorder or of a psychiatric assessment having been done during this period. His sickness did not prevent him from starting yet another job – this time at the Home Office. He did not mention to them he was ill, nor did he tell them he was working elsewhere. Unsurprisingly, a succession of his line managers told the jury he had not been very good at his jobs. Especially damning was the evidence given by Dan McCartney, who managed Chowdhury at Defra. He said he had to "effectively tell him what to do the whole time" and that Chowdhury kept his camera off during video calls for four months, claiming technical problems. But because Chowdhury was not subject to any formal performance measures at Defra, he was given a permanent job. He remained there for two years. In September 2023, Chowdhury was found to have more than £40,000 in his bank accounts as well as significant investments, including £45,000 in premium bonds. 'Risk averse' Civil Service A recent survey of 1,700 civil servants by the independent think tank Re:State found 76% of respondents thought it did not do a good job of tackling poor performers. An ex-senior civil servant told the BBC that much of the Civil Service is culturally averse to performance management. "Whitehall's known for ages it has to be less risk averse. Shrinking the Civil Service and the adoption of artificial intelligence technology make that more vital," they said. "But don't underestimate the fear factor: fear of drawn-out grievances and fear of being accused of wasting taxpayers' money if the Civil Service was to do what big private sector firms do, which is cut to get rid of poor performers by offering some money and a settlement agreement." A Defra spokesperson said: "Kashim Chowdhury abused the trust placed in him as a public servant and defrauded taxpayers out of almost £285,000. He will now rightly face the consequences for his actions. "This conviction is the result of a thorough and painstaking investigation led by the Defra Counter Fraud and Investigations team. It sends a clear message that fraud against the public purse will not be tolerated and those responsible will be held to account." The spokesperson said Defra would use "all available avenues to recover the proceeds of Chowdhury's offending on behalf of taxpayers". Chowdhury's case also illustrates a wider issue. He was engaged in what is being called "polygamous working", where people hold down several jobs secretly. Websites have even been set up offering people advice on how to keep their employers in the dark. Its rise has been blamed on larger numbers of people working from home. The government's National Fraud Initiative has identified 23 cases of "polygamous working" across London in its most recent report. It uncovered £500,000 of overpaid salaries over a period of a few months. Alongside the fraud case, Chowdhury is involved in a legal dispute with his three siblings, who accuse him of ''bullying'' their mother into signing over half of her £2.1m home to him in the final days of her life. He denies it. At times during his criminal trial, Chowdhury appeared confused by what he was hearing and blamed trauma for the web of lies he had spun. The jury took seven hours to reach their verdict and decided he was motivated by personal gain - stealing tens of thousands of pounds from the taxpayer. Chowdhury now faces a significant custodial sentence. Related topics - Published2 hours ago

items.articleText: Türk Altın'ın (TRALT) 3. çeyrek kârı beklentileri neredeyse ikiye katladı! İşte detaylar - Türk Altın İşletmeleri, 2026'nın üçüncü çeyreğinde 2,49 milyar TL net kâr açıkladı. Şirketin çeyreklik kârı, 8 aracı kurumun 1,30 milyar TL'lik ortalama beklentisini yüzde 91 aştı. Türk Altın İşletmeleri A.Ş. (TRALT), 2026 yılı üçüncü çeyrek finansal sonuçlarını Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu'nda (KAP) açıkladı. Eski unvanıyla Koza Altın İşletmeleri olarak bilinen şirket, yılın üçüncü çeyreğinde 2 milyar 490 milyon 253 bin TL net kâr elde etti. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Şirketin üçüncü çeyrek kârı, analist beklentilerinin oldukça üzerinde gerçekleşti. Matriks Haber tarafından düzenlenen bilanço anketine katılan 8 kurumun ortalama net kâr tahmini 1 milyar 303 milyon 200 bin TL, medyan beklentisi ise 1 milyar 254 milyon 400 bin TL seviyesindeydi. Böylece TRALT, ortalama beklentiyi yaklaşık yüzde 91 oranında aştı. 9 aylık net kâr yüzde 7 geriledi Türk Altın İşletmeleri, 1 Ocak-30 Eylül 2026 döneminde toplam 5 milyar 482 milyon 827 bin TL net kâr açıkladı. Şirketin geçen yılın aynı dönemindeki net kârı 5 milyar 922 milyon 218 bin TL olmuştu. Buna göre 9 aylık net kâr yıllık bazda yüzde 7 azaldı. items.titleTr: Republican congressman to force impeachment vote on Defence Secretary Hegseth
items.summaryTr: The effort will likely fail, but Representative Thomas Massie wants to push Trump to fire Hegseth before Democrats can launch their own impeachment process.
items.articleText: Republican congressman to force impeachment vote on Defence Secretary Hegseth - Published A Republican congressman plans to force a vote in the House of Representatives this week to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, alleging he has violated the US Constitution. "By engaging in hostilities in Iran for more than 90 days without congressional authorization, Secretary Hegseth is breaking the law and must be held accountable," Representative Thomas Massie said. The effort will likely fail, given Republicans will remain in power in Congress until January. But Massie says he wants to push President Donald Trump to fire Hegseth before Democrats can launch an impeachment process. Hegseth, who will hold a news conference on Tuesday about Massie's move, said he was not concerned. "We're not worried about that," Hegseth said when asked by reporters about the impending resolution on Monday, adding he would hold a news conference Tuesday morning "on that very topic". Hegseth's last news conference was in May. Massie, who lost re-election earlier this year, is among the few Republicans who have been critical of Trump and the war that started earlier in this year in Iran. The Kentucky congressman first introduced impeachment articles in September and is now pressing for a vote in the wake of Republicans losing control of both the House and Senate in last week's midterm elections. He has said his push to rid the administration of Hegseth is meant to prevent a Democrat spectacle next year. "My effort to impeach Secretary Hegseth is a much gentler version of what's coming when the Democrats assume control of the House and Senate next year," Massie also said in a statement. "They will hold hearings and trials." "President Trump should replace Secretary Hegseth now while he can still get a replacement confirmed in the Senate," he also said. Impeaching a cabinet secretary is very rare. The impeachment must be approved by both chambers for the secretary to be removed from office. The House has voted to impeach only two cabinet members in US history, but the Senate did not agree on either one. Once Massie introduces his resolution - expected later on Monday - Speaker of the House Mike Johnson must schedule a time to consider it within two days. Along with voting on the resolution directly, the House has the option to vote to refer it to committee or to set it aside. Massie will likely have the support of the Democrats in the House, with that party's leader, Hakeem Jeffries, saying on Sunday that he is a "hard yes" on impeachment. But Massie would still need to win over members of his own party. The House has passed a War Powers resolution - a measure that seeks to halt Trump from taking further military action in Iran - multiple times this year, with Massie's support. But Massie's disagreement with Hegseth also goes beyond Iran, he said in the statement. He has accused Hegseth of intimidating critics of the Trump administration, kidnapping foreign leaders and ignoring congressional war powers resolutions. Related topics - Published17 hours ago

items.articleText: Dev kurumdan bitcoin analizi: Saldırılara rağmen piyasa direnç gösterdi Binance'e yönelik 6,3 milyar dolarlık siber saldırının ardından Bitcoin'deki düşüş yüzde 6 ile sınırlı kaldı. Fitch Ratings, bu tabloyu kripto piyasasının daha dayanıklı hale geldiğine işaret eden bir gelişme olarak değerlendirdi. Binance'e 6,3 milyar dolarlık saldırı 29 Ekim'de başlayan siber saldırıda Binance'ten yaklaşık 6,3 milyar dolar değerinde dijital varlık çalındı. Olay, bugüne kadarki en büyük kripto para hırsızlıklarından biri olarak değerlendirildi. İşlemler geçici olarak durduruldu Saldırının ardından Binance, alım satım ve para çekme işlemlerini geçici olarak durdurdu. Para çekme hizmetleri 1 Kasım'da yeniden başlatıldı. Bitcoin'de düşüş yüzde 6'da kaldı Saldırıya ilişkin ilk haberlerin ardından Bitcoin, yaklaşık 10 saat içinde yüzde 6 değer kaybetti. Günlük işlem hacmi ise yüzde 67 arttı. Fitch Ratings, fiyat hareketinin geçmişte yaşanan büyük piyasa şoklarına kıyasla sınırlı kaldığına dikkat çekti. Fitch: Piyasa altyapısı daha dayanıklı hale geldi Fitch, kripto para alım satım piyasalarının daha derin ve çeşitlendirilmiş bir yapıya kavuşmasının bu sınırlı tepkinin nedenlerinden biri olduğunu değerlendirdi. Kurum, tek bir borsaya bağımlılığın azalmasının, belirli bir platformda yaşanan aksaklıklara rağmen piyasa likiditesini desteklediğini belirtti. Bitcoin destekli menkul kıymetler için görüş değişmedi Fitch, saldırının tek başına Bitcoin destekli menkul kıymetlere ilişkin analitik değerlendirmesini değiştirmediğini açıkladı. Kurum, daha sınırlı piyasa tepkisinin Bitcoin piyasasının likidite ve altyapı bakımından olgunlaştığına dair kanıtlara katkı sağlayabileceğini, ancak bunun fiyat, işlem hacmi ve piyasa derinliği analizleriyle desteklenmesi gerektiğini vurguladı.

items.title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy
items.summary: The share price dropped wiped hundreds of billions of dollars from the value of Nvidia.

items.titleTr: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy
items.summaryTr: The share price dropped wiped hundreds of billions of dollars from the value of Nvidia.
items.articleText: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy - Published Hundreds of billions of dollars have been wiped off the value of Nvidia after the US chipmaker announced an independent investigation would be carried out into its chief executive's affair with an alleged Chinese spy. The tech firm saw its shares fall by about 6% on Monday after Jensen Huang admitted having an extramarital affair. Nvidia's probe came after reports that the US believed the Nvidia boss had been targeted in an espionage campaign by China. However, China has rejected the claims, with its foreign ministry saying "allegations about Chinese spies were "entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China". Nvidia said it had no reason to believe the company's secrets or national security were compromised, but a statement by the firm's board of directors said it would begin an investigation in "light of recent reporting that founder and chief executive Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort". US intelligence officials believe Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, was a spy for Beijing, according to a New York Times report, external. The report said Secretary of State Marco Rubio sent a memo to top officials in Washington last spring warning that the Nvidia boss was in a close relationship with a Chinese spy. Alice Huang was managing director of Singaporean company Megaspeed, which has had dealings with Nvidia. Huang admitted he was "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting her and their children. He added he was "committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America's national security" and would cooperate with the investigation. After the investigation was announced, other big tech bosses, including Elon Musk, came out in support of Huang to continue leading the firm. US President Donald Trump said the Nvidia boss was an "honourable guy". However, the news sparked a sell-off in Nvidia's shares, with about $250bn (£190bn) wiped of the company's market value. While Nvidia shares fell, the US stock market opened on a positive note on Monday after last week's turmoil, with Nvidia's rival chipmakers benefiting. But analysts suggested the hit to the company would be short-lived. Victoria Fernandez, chief market strategist at Crossmark Global Investments said investors would not abandon Nvidia, because the chipmaker was so central to the AI industry. "Nvidia is the core of this AI trade, and without them, all these other pieces start to fall apart because the financing's not there," she told the BBC. Huang co-founded Nvidia, which is central to making the hardware for emerging AI technologies, with two other engineers in 1993. Its chips were initially designed for gaming, but Huang decided to turn its focus on AI development, turning it into the world's second most valuable company. Huang's position vulnerable unlike other tech bosses A key concern for investors going forward is what would happen to Nvidia if Huang was removed from the company, as Fernandez said there was "no natural successor" to the chief executive. Huang, unlike other founders in the tech industry, is vulnerable to any move by Nvidia's board of directors to oust him. He owns only around 3.5% of the company, and Nvidia operates on a single class voting structure, meaning his stake would not be enough to act as a veto power over any board decision. By contrast, many tech founders who lead their companies, including Mark Zuckerberg of Meta and Musk of Tesla and SpaceX, hold significant percentages of multiple types of stock in their companies. Fernandez said she does not believe the board will remove Huang as chief executive, unless there is glaring evidence of wrongdoing related to national security or intellectual property, "but I bet they start bringing someone up as his number two, to have there for the future." The modest fall in its shares mean investors believe it is unlikely he will step down or be removed as chief executive, but that the outcome of the investigation will be closely watched. Even people who do not directly own shares in Nvidia can be affected by rises and falls in its value. Pensions or savings invested in pots which have stakes in the company through index tracking funds can be impacted, for example. - What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy - Published3 hours ago Nvidia chips have been a major focus of the AI race between the US and China and the White House has previously imposed controls on where its advanced products can be sold. The H200, Nvidia's second most advanced semiconductor, had previously been restricted by Washington over concerns that it would give China's technology industry an edge over the US. But Huang has been against restricting the sale of Nvidia's chips to China, arguing that it would be better for the global rollout of AI to be powered by US technology. In January, the Trump administration said it would allow the company to sell its H200 chips to Chinese customers under certain conditions. Additional reporter by Samira Hussain, North America business correspondent.

items.summaryTr: The outlet has been evicted from its offices of three decades and says it's been blocked from receiving donations.
items.articleText: Russia's leading independent newspaper closes after eviction Russia's leading independent newspaper has closed after being evicted from its offices and facing pressure from authorities. For 30 years, Novaya Gazeta published investigations into corruption, human rights violations and abuse of power in the country. On Monday, the team behind the newspaper had a final editorial meeting before packing up their belongings and leaving. The Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Russia's media was highly diverse and that the newspaper's closure was part of "a standard rotational process". The BBC spoke to its co-founder Dmitry Muratov, a Nobel Peace Prize winner, about the closure.

items.articleText: Trump'tan ABD seçim sistemine tepki: “Bu sistemle seçim kazanmak imkansız” - ABD Başkanı Donald Trump, Kongre ara seçimlerinde kullanılan elektronik oy makinelerini ve erken oy verme sürecini eleştirdi. Trump, seçim sistemindeki mevcut koşullarda kazanmanın “imkânsız” olduğunu savundu. ABD Başkanı Donald Trump, Truth Social hesabından yaptığı paylaşımda ABD'deki seçim sistemini hedef aldı. Kongre ara seçimleri öncesinde elektronik oy makineleri ve erken oy kullanma süreçlerine yönelik eleştirilerini yineleyen Trump, seçimlerin güvenilirliğini sorguladı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Trump, “Bu seçimin dürüst olduğuna gerçekten inanan var mı?” ifadelerini kullanarak elektronik oy makinelerinin seçim sisteminde seçmenden daha önemli hale geldiğini öne sürdü. Trump erken oy kullanma sürecini hedef aldı Seçim öncesinde yayımlanan anket sonuçlarına da değinen Trump, anketlerin bu kadar yanılmış olamayacağını savundu. Erken oy kullanma sürecine ilişkin eleştirilerini sürdüren Trump, bazı toplu oy girişlerinin büyüklüğüne dikkat çekerek, “Erken oy kullanma sürecindeki bazı toplu girişler o kadar büyüktü ki, kaç kişi oy vermeye giderse gitsin, kazanmak imkânsızdı” dedi. Trump, bu açıklamalarıyla ABD'de seçimlerin yürütülme biçimine yönelik itirazlarını yeniden gündeme taşıdı. Trump'ın 2020 seçimlerine ilişkin iddiaları kanıtlanamamıştı Trump, 2020 başkanlık seçimlerinde Demokrat aday Joe Biden'a karşı kaybetmesinin ardından da elektronik oy makinelerini, posta yoluyla oy kullanma yöntemini ve erken oy sürecini eleştirmişti. Trump ve bazı Cumhuriyetçi destekçileri, Dominion Voting Systems gibi şirketlerin geliştirdiği elektronik oylama sistemlerinin manipülasyona açık olduğunu öne sürmüştü. Seçimlerde sistematik hile yapıldığı iddiasıyla Trump ve kampanya ekibi tarafından çok sayıda dava açılmış, ancak bu iddiaları destekleyen somut kanıtlar sunulamadığı gerekçesiyle davaların neredeyse tamamı mahkemeler tarafından reddedilmişti.

items.summaryTr: Eyewitnesses say the explosion shook the ground, with one believing an earthquake had hit near the Habas Demir Celik plant in Aliaga.
items.articleText: Turkey steel factory blast kills at least 16 people - Published At least 16 people have died and 13 others have been injured in an explosion at an iron and steel factory near the port city of Izmir in western Turkey. All those killed and injured were workers at the Habas plant, one of the country's leading steel producers, authorities said. Footage from the scene showed a large fire inside the facility and a towering column of smoke rising into the air. The local governor said the blast happened around midday after a crane carrying a replacement boiler collapsed, causing materials to fall into a furnace below. Workplace accidents remain a chronic problem in Turkey, the Turkish Health and Safety Labor Watch, an independent civil society organisation, said. Eyewitnesses said the explosion shook the ground, with one person initially believing an earthquake had struck. In a statement, the company said the accident occurred during scheduled maintenance work on one of the plant's electric arc furnaces. Izmir Governor Süleyman Elban told media that some people are believed to be still under the rubble. Speaking after a cabinet meeting on Monday, Turkey's President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan confirmed the deaths and said investigations were under way, while search and rescue operations continued. He also said two of the injured were in a serious condition. At least five people have been arrested, according BBC News's Turkish service, citing local media reports. The Habas plant is in the Izmir district of Aliaga which is a major port and one of Turkey's main shipbreaking hubs. - Published29 October - Published15 October

(CWENE), 2026 yılı üçüncü çeyrek finansal sonuçlarını 9 Kasım'da Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu'nda (KAP) yayımladı. items.articleText: PNC Bank tests turning USDC payments into dollar deposits The pilot lets eligible corporate and institutional clients accept USDC on Ethereum, with each token converted to one US dollar before deposit. PNC Bank, the eighth-largest US bank by assets, launched a limited pilot enabling eligible corporate and institutional clients to receive USDC payments through Coinbase. The pilot accepts USDC, a US dollar-backed stablecoin issued by Circle, on Ethereum using Coinbase Payments products. Payments are automatically converted into dollars and deposited into designated PNC accounts, allowing businesses to accept stablecoins without holding them. PNC said the service aims to speed up access to funds and improve cross-border payment efficiency. The bank did not disclose fees, settlement-time benchmarks or the number of participating clients, nor did it respond to Cointelegraph’s request for additional details by publication time. The pilot builds on a partnership established in July 2025, when PNC agreed to offer cryptocurrency services through Coinbase’s infrastructure while providing banking services to the exchange. The partnership led to the launch of Bitcoin (BTC) trading for eligible PNC Private Bank clients in December. PNC’s move follows a similar initiative by Citi, which expanded its Coinbase partnership in September to enable institutional clients to accept stablecoin payments through its Spring by Citi platform, with Coinbase converting the payments into fiat currency. USDC is the second-largest stablecoin by market capitalization, at $70.5 billion, behind Tether’s USDT at $176.8 billion, according to DefiLlama data. The total stablecoin market stood at around $290.8 billion on Monday. Magazine: Vitalik ‘pivots’ ETH to store of value, crypto suffers after US midterms: Hodler’s Digest

items.titleTr: Trump questions midterm elections integrity after previously accepting results
items.summaryTr: Trump made the claims, without evidence, on Truth Social on Monday.
items.articleText: Trump questions midterm elections integrity after previously accepting results - Published US President Donald Trump has questioned the legitimacy of the midterm election results in which Republicans suffered sweeping losses, days after saying he would accept the outcome. "Does anybody really believe that this 'Election' was honest. How could the Polls be so wrong?" Trump wrote on Truth Social on Monday. This appeared to contradict what he told the New York Times on election night that he was "absolutely willing" to accept the results. Democrats retook both chambers of Congress in last week's elections. State and local officials across the US said voting had been mostly problem-free. Some key races, including Senate contests in Alaska and Mississippi, have yet to be called. In the Truth Social post, Trump made vague claims about polling, voting "dumps", and "machines" without providing specific evidence of what this referred to and whether he believed there had been error or wrongdoing. The reporting of vote counts on election night proceeded as normal, according to Charles Stewart III, a political scientist at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT). "We saw across the nation the standard patterns we see in terms of when the votes are reported," he said. Stewart added that in some states, like Florida and Georgia, some initial reporting of results happens quickly because they already have the results of early and mail ballots. Trump has previously attempted to cast doubts on the integrity of elections he has lost, although he himself was not on the ballot in the midterms. "We would have won easily if I was on the ballot," Trump told CBS News, the BBC's US partner, after it was confirmed his party had lost both the Senate and the House. Surveys ahead of the election from several pollsters and news outlets suggested that Republicans could lose seats in both the House and Senate. As it stands, Democrats have won 54 US Senate seats and 254 US House seats in the midterms, giving them comfortable majorities in both chambers of Congress even as counting continues in some races, like in Alaska and Mississippi. "State laws and practicalities are such that some states will just take longer to count," said Ruth Greenwood, director of the Election Law Clinic at Harvard Law School. "That doesn't mean anything nefarious is occurring—we just need to trust local election officials to count every vote and tell us the results when they are done." The outcome has been clear since election night. Trump told the New York Times then: "We'll, you know, look forward to working with [Democrats]", adding: "We'll probably work something out." He has also offered his own analysis of why Republicans lost, acknowledging on Fox News that the Iran war had contributed to the defeat. "People agree with what I'm doing on Iran but they really probably weren't willing to do the short term consequences of paying more for gasoline - I understand that," he said. Vice-President JD Vance has also blamed the Iran war, which began in February and which has severely disrupted global oil and gas supplies - causing costs to soar, as the reason their party lost the election. In the run-up to the midterms, Trump made claims about widespread voting fraud, despite evidence that it is rare. He and his allies alleged for months that the 2020 presidential election, which he lost to former President Joe Biden, had been rigged against him. His lawyers and allies spent weeks attempting to litigate the results, but courts repeatedly struck them down. The justice department during his administration has made unprecedented attempts to exert more federal control over elections - a power the Constitution primarily delegates to individual states. Days before these midterms, it filed controversial lawsuits in federal courts challenging the count and certification of votes in states like California and Alaska, but judges ruled against them in nearly all instances. Election law experts, state officials, and local elections offices told the BBC they had spent months preparing for a scenario in which the White House or election sceptics questioned the votes' legitimacy. Despite the intense focus around election integrity on both sides of the debate, top state and local election officials have reported a mostly smooth process so far for the 2026 midterms. Extreme weather did force some location closures, and a handful of reported administrative or technical issues slowed the process in some local jurisdictions.

items.title: Avalanche’s AVAX leads crypto gains following NYSE tokenization deal
items.summary: Avalanche’s AVAX token rose as much as 10% after the NYSE selected its blockchain to support settlement on a planned tokenized stock trading platform.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Avalanche’s AVAX leads crypto gains following NYSE tokenization deal
items.summaryTr: Avalanche’s AVAX token rose as much as 10% after the NYSE selected its blockchain to support settlement on a planned tokenized stock trading platform.
items.articleText: Avalanche’s AVAX leads crypto gains following NYSE tokenization deal Avalanche’s AVAX token rose as much as 10% after the NYSE selected its blockchain to support settlement on a planned tokenized stock trading platform. Avalanche’s AVAX token jumped as much as 10% on Monday, making it the top earner among the 100 largest cryptocurrencies by market capitalization, as the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) announced plans to use its blockchain to settle trades on a new platform for trading tokenized stocks around the clock. AVAX later eased to $8.86, still up over 8% on the day, according to CoinGecko data as of 03:22 p.m. UTC. The token currently has a market cap of around $3.95 billion, with $439.7 million traded over the past day. The Avalanche blockchain boasts a total value locked (TVL) of $633 million, up 4% over the past 24 hours, according to DeFiLlama. “At the NYSE, we’re looking at how blockchain technology can expand what we offer in equities, and we’re picking the right technology for each job,” Dennis Lee, the head of digital issuance at NYSE, said in an announcement. The deal underscores a growing effort by Wall Street firms to use blockchain technology to make stock trading faster and allow investors to trade outside regular market hours. Typically, traditional US stock markets are open from 9:30 am to 4:00 pm EST on weekdays, with trades often taking at least one business day to settle. The NYSE first announced plans for the platform in January. In September, Ava Labs revealed that the exchange had spent about a year testing Avalanche, but the blockchain’s final pick was not confirmed until Monday. Related: Aave launches V4 on Avalanche, laying groundwork for tokenized credit markets NYSE chooses Avalanche Ava Labs said that the NYSE will use Avalanche’s blockchain to keep track of stock trades and help complete transactions on its planned trading platform. The platform will let investors buy and sell digital versions of stocks on different blockchains, while Avalanche will be used to record those trades and make sure transactions are completed. “The upcoming digital trading platform will support equities listed on a range of blockchains, though the ledger that records and settles trades needs to be fast and reliable, let us control who can take part, keep costs predictable, and have a large community of developers behind it. Avalanche meets all those needs,” Lee said. The platform could launch before the end of 2026 if it receives regulatory approval, according to The Wall Street Journal. “Our first conversations with the NYSE team began nearly a year ago, and it’s remarkable how quickly we’ve progressed toward supporting this infrastructure,” John Nahas, chief business officer at Ava Labs told Cointelegraph. “It’s an important step toward blockchain becoming foundational financial infrastructure.” Wall Street dives into tokenized stocks The news comes as other major financial firms are also investing in blockchain technology to make stock trading faster and available around the clock. In September, Nasdaq announced plans to invest $100 million in Kraken’s parent company, Payward, to launch tokenized stocks. The expected launch for that project is the second quarter of 2027. Meanwhile, the Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC), which helps settle US securities trades, launched a service in October that allows financial firms to turn traditional securities into digital tokens. “Today marks the culmination of years of work to bring tokenized securities into a regulated framework supported by trusted market infrastructure,” Frank La Salla, CEO of DTCC, said at the time. “By extending DTC’s resiliency, governance and operational standards into digital markets, we are establishing the foundation for responsible institutional adoption at scale.” The NYSE deal also follows other financial firms’ efforts to bring traditional financial assets specifically onto Avalanche. In July, Japanese financial technology company Progmat announced it had moved more than 452 billion yen worth of digital securities onto a dedicated Avalanche blockchain. And in September, Aave Labs announced plans to launch a lending service on Avalanche that would let financial firms borrow Tether’s USAT stablecoin using tokenized assets as collateral. items.title: Civil servant who secretly held five jobs found guilty of fraud
items.summary: Kashim Chowdhury had secretly held multiple public sector jobs on full-time salaries.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Civil servant who secretly held five jobs found guilty of fraud
items.summaryTr: Kashim Chowdhury had secretly held multiple public sector jobs on full-time salaries.
items.articleText: Civil servant who secretly held five jobs found guilty of fraud - Published A civil servant who secretly held multiple public sector jobs on full-time salaries has been found guilty of nine counts of fraud. Kashim Chowdhury, from east London, had five government jobs that overlapped in the spring of 2023. He fraudulently earned more than £284,000 of taxpayers' money. The prosecution accused the 56-year-old of ''deliberate, intentional dishonesty'' and of ''exploiting the system''. After seven hours of deliberation, the jury unanimously found Chowdhury guilty of eight counts of fraud by false representation and one count of fraud by a failure to disclose. The judge said Chowdhury faced a ''very significant custodial sentence''. He added he was refusing bail because of the significance of the crime and for Chowdhury's own wellbeing. 'Abused trust' "This was sustained and deliberate dishonesty," said Sarah Melo, specialist prosecutor at the CPS Serious Economic Organised Crime and International Directorate. "He knew he could not legitimately hold multiple full-time positions at the same time, but continued to conceal what he was doing." A Defra spokesperson said Chowdury "abused the trust placed in him as a public servant", adding that it would use all available avenues to recover the proceeds of Chowdhury's offending. Between 2020 and 2023 Chowdhury had eight full-time public sector roles that overlapped and earned him £350,000 in total. The prosecution told the court that on application forms he provided inaccurate information about his employment status and failed to disclose to government departments that he was already a civil servant. Once he secured the roles he didn't tell his employers he was working elsewhere. He was allowed to work entirely from home because he told his employers he was caring for his mother, whom he lived with in east London. She had dementia and was diagnosed with terminal cancer in 2023. - How a civil servant got away with juggling five jobs for so long - Published55 minutes ago But rather than reduce his workload to look after her, he kept taking on new jobs. In the spring of 2023, when his mother was a few months away from death, he had jobs at the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs, the Department of Health and Social Care, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), the Department for Business and Trade, the Food Standards Agency and the Home Office. During this period he was contracted to work 183 hours a week - more than the number of hours that exist in seven days. Chowdhury said he had taken on so many roles because he feared losing his livelihood after experiencing insecure employment in the past. He was made redundant from a job at the Department for Education in 2013 and was given a diagnosis of PTSD. He said he had not been thinking clearly when applying for jobs ''because of my stress, distress and trauma and due to my panic at the time". But the prosecution barrister, Lucy Organ, told the jury: "He's lied to you in evidence, he's lied to you under oath, which demonstrates the level of deceit he has descended to." A succession of his managers told the court about his poor performance. Especially damning was the evidence given by Dan McCartney who managed Chowdhury at Defra. He said he had to "effectively tell him what to do the whole time". McCartney said that during video calls Chowdhury had his camera switched off blaming technical problems. McCartney said this went on for four to five months. But McCartney said that because Chowdhury was not subject to any formal performance measures at Defra, he was given a permanent job and remained there for two years. The prosecution argued that he used sick notes to cope with his impossible schedule. In March 2023, he was on sick leave from four of the organisations he worked for. But he kept working at the Home Office and did not tell them he was ill. His line manager at the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), Aleesha Adams, organised a video call with him in May 2023. By this point he'd been off sick for three months and she wanted to make a plan to get him back to work. She told the jury that at the start of the call he was coughing a lot and waving tissues up to the camera. She also told the jury that he had been wearing white make-up to try to look ill. Adams told the court that as the meeting went on the make-up started coming off his forehead. ''He was sweating, it was like rubbing off so it was darker underneath and darker on the neck." Chowdhury told the jury this was a smear and that he had not been wearing make-up. After the call, Adams discovered that he had logged into the call using a Defra email address. When she challenged him about it he blamed a technical error. Adams grew suspicious. ''I believed he was lying,'' she told the jury. She escalated her concerns up the chain at the UKHSA. But his fraudulent behaviour went on for several more months until he left the civil service in September 2023. He was finally caught in 2024 by the government's National Fraud Initiative, which conducts searches of civil service databases such as payroll every two years to look for anomalies. Chowdhury has also been accused by his siblings of bullying their mother into increasing his share of the family home days before she died. In a case at the High Court, Chowdhury's two brothers and sister allege that he put "undue influence" on Faijun Nessa to sign documents that meant he would inherit half of her home. The four-storey, six-bedroom home in east London has been valued at £2.1m. His siblings say their mother could not have understood what she was signing because she was "desperately unwell". In January 2023 she was given a terminal diagnosis of stage four metastatic colorectal cancer. The claimants also allege that Mrs Nessa, who was nearly blind and could not speak English, was unaware of what she was signing because the documents were not translated into her native Bengali at the time they were signed. Kashim Chowdhury denies the claims. That case is ongoing.

The claimants also allege that Mrs Nessa, who was nearly blind and could not speak English, was unaware of what she was signing because the documents were not translated into her native Bengali at the time they were signed. Kashim Chowdhury denies the claims. That case is ongoing.

items.articleText: Pegasus'un (PGSUS) 3. çeyrekte beklentileri aştı: İşte bilanço detayları! - Pegasus, 2026'nın üçüncü çeyreğinde 11,27 milyar TL net kâr açıkladı. Ancak yılın ilk yarısındaki zarar nedeniyle şirketin 9 aylık toplam net sonucu 1,28 milyar TL zarar oldu. Üçüncü çeyrek kârı piyasa beklentilerini aştı. Pegasus Hava Taşımacılığı A.Ş. (PGSUS), 2026 yılı üçüncü çeyrek finansal sonuçlarını 9 Kasım'da Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu'nda (KAP) yayımladı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Şirket, 1 Ocak-30 Eylül 2026 döneminde 1 milyar 279 milyon 203 bin TL net zarar açıkladı. Pegasus, 2025'in aynı döneminde 13 milyar 326 milyon 666 bin TL net kâr elde etmişti. Buna karşın şirket, yalnızca 2026'nın üçüncü çeyreğinde 11 milyar 272 milyon 632 bin TL net kâr kaydetti. Satış gelirleri yüzde 32 arttı Pegasus'un ilk 9 aylık hasılatı, geçen yılın aynı dönemindeki 114 milyar 405 milyon 95 bin TL'den 150 milyar 626 milyon 803 bin TL'ye yükseldi. Böylece satış gelirlerinde yıllık bazda yüzde 32 artış gerçekleşti. Şirketin esas faaliyet kârı ise aynı dönemde 10 milyar 872 milyon 782 bin TL'den 9 milyar 359 milyon 283 bin TL'ye geriledi. FAVÖK, 2025'in ilk 9 ayında 30 milyar 246 milyon 178 bin TL seviyesindeyken, 2026'nın aynı döneminde 26 milyar 518 milyon 410 bin TL olarak gerçekleşti. Pegasus'un varlıkları 492 milyar TL'yi aştı Şirketin toplam varlıkları 2025 yıl sonundaki 410 milyar 168 milyon 212 bin TL'den 2026'nın üçüncü çeyreği sonunda 492 milyar 104 milyon 652 bin TL'ye yükseldi. Aynı dönemde toplam borçlar 293 milyar 314 milyon 340 bin TL'den 360 milyar 369 milyon 107 bin TL'ye çıktı. Özkaynaklar ise 116 milyar 853 milyon 872 bin TL'den 131 milyar 735 milyon 545 bin TL'ye ulaştı. Pegasus'un piyasa değeri 73,25 milyar TL, PD/DD oranı ise 0,56 olarak açıklandı. Pegasus bilançosu beklentileri aştı Matriks Haber tarafından gerçekleştirilen bilanço anketine 15 aracı kurum katıldı. Ankete göre Pegasus'un üçüncü çeyrek net kârına ilişkin ortalama beklenti 8 milyar 895 milyon 300 bin TL, medyan beklenti ise 8 milyar 834 milyon TL oldu. Şirketin açıkladığı 11 milyar 272 milyon 632 bin TL'lik üçüncü çeyrek net kârı, hem ortalama hem de medyan beklentinin üzerinde gerçekleşti.

items.title: Nine Zimbabweans caught allegedly trying to leave South Africa to fight in Ukraine
items.summary: Hundreds of people from different African countries have been recruited to fight for Russia, according to Ukraine.

items.titleTr: Nine Zimbabweans caught allegedly trying to leave South Africa to fight in Ukraine
items.summaryTr: Hundreds of people from different African countries have been recruited to fight for Russia, according to Ukraine.
items.articleText: Nine Zimbabweans caught allegedly trying to leave South Africa to fight in Ukraine - Published Nine Zimbabweans have been arrested in South Africa after they were caught allegedly trying to leave the country to fight in the war between Russia and the Ukraine, police say. The group, aged between 20 and 26, were arrested in and around Johannesburg by a multidisciplinary team on Sunday evening. They were caught as they were "preparing to board flights out of the country", authorities added, but their final destination is unclear. They have been charged with contravening South Africa's Regulation of Foreign Military Assistance Act, which outlaws mercenary activity without government permission. Police said five people were arrested at South Africa's biggest airport, OR Tambo, and another four at a hotel in Bruma, east of Johannesburg by a multidisciplinary team that involved Interpol. All nine later appeared in court, according to state prosecutors. The police statement added that the involvement of Interpol and other international law enforcement agencies indicated that the suspects had also allegedly violated laws in their respective home countries, prompting cooperation with South African authorities. They have also not said whether the group allegedly intended to fight for Russia or Ukraine nor provided details of the organisations allegedly involved in facilitating their travel. Citizens of several African countries, including Kenya, Ghana and South Africa, have gone to fight for Russia in Ukraine - some they had been duped and had not realised where they were going. A Ukrainian intelligence assessment estimated earlier this year that more than 1,700 people from 36 countries in Africa have been recruited to fight for Russia. Kenya at the time estimated that 252 citizens had been illegally conscripted in Russia. In March, Foreign Minister Musalia Mudavadi visited Moscow to address the issue. He said at the time that an agreement had been reached to stop recruiting Kenyan nationals. In March, Zimbabwe said that 15 of its nationals had been killed after being recruited to fight for Russia in Ukraine, with more than 60 still trapped on the frontlines. The previous month, South Africa secured the return of 17 South Africans who were allegedly tricked into joining the war. In December last year, South African authorities arrested five people, including a journalist, for allegedly recruiting people to join the war. Ukraine has also been recruiting foreign nationals, including from Africa. items.titleTr: Watch: Rare insight into France's drug gangs recruiting children to commit violence
items.summaryTr: "It destroys people, but we all make our own choices" - Marseille drug-gang members spoke to the BBC.
items.articleText: Watch: Rare insight into France's drug gangs recruiting children to commit violence A BBC investigation has found one of Europe's most powerful drug gangs in France is recruiting teenage children from across the country to commit kidnap and murder. Known as the "DZ Mafia", the gang won a bloody turf war against a rival group in Marseille during 2023, and is now recruiting from further afield. One member who is in prison awaiting trial after being implicated in several murders told the BBC he was part of a DZ Mafia hit squad. He agrees the killings he has been charged with were "quite shocking". "Attempts in broad daylight, in traffic jams… it can range from going to hit a guy, slap him to taking him in front of his mother and burning him up in a car. I think I have good composure, I handle it fairly well." When challenged over whether he feels regret when carrying out such acts of brutality, he says he feels "guilty in-part" but claims to have no regrets. Like so many teenagers from Marseille, he knew large sums of money could be earned quickly in drug trafficking. Now in his twenties, he admits the environment he entered was a "trap". The BBC's Paris Correspondent, James Waterhouse, reports from Marseille.

items.articleText: Erdoğan'dan emekli maaşları için yeni mesaj: “Mali imkanları oluşturuyoruz” - Cumhurbaşkanı Erdoğan, fon soruşturmasına ilişkin “Taviz yok” mesajı verirken emeklilerin durumunu iyileştirecek mali imkanlar üzerinde çalışıldığını söyledi. Gabar'da iki yeni sahadan daha olumlu haber geldiğini belirten Erdoğan, petrol üretimi ve enerji hedeflerine ilişkin açıklamalarda bulundu. Cumhurbaşkanı Recep Tayyip Erdoğan başkanlığında gerçekleştirilen Kabine toplantısının ardından ekonomi gündemine ilişkin açıklamalar yapıldı. Erdoğan, fon soruşturmasının yakından takip edildiğini belirtirken emekli aylıklarına yönelik yeni düzenleme çalışmalarına ve Gabar'daki petrol faaliyetlerine de değindi. Fon soruşturmasında “taviz yok” mesajı CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Cumhurbaşkanı Erdoğan, fon soruşturmasına ilişkin sürecin yakından takip edildiğini belirterek, “Meseleyi çok sıkı bir şekilde takip ediyoruz. Vatandaşlarımız bize güvenmeye devam etsin” ifadelerini kullandı. Erdoğan'ın açıklaması, soruşturmanın kararlılıkla sürdürüleceği mesajı olarak öne çıktı. Emekli maaşlarına ek zam hazırlığı Kabine toplantısının gündeminde emekli aylıklarına yönelik düzenleme de yer aldı. Erdoğan, emeklilerin ekonomik durumunu iyileştirmeye yönelik çalışmalar hakkında, “Emeklilerimizin durumunu biraz daha iyileştirecek mali imkanları oluşturuyoruz” dedi. Emeklilere enflasyon farkının yanı sıra ek refah payı verilmesine yönelik çalışmalar sürüyor. Hazırlanan taslakların Erdoğan'a sunulmasının ardından düzenlemenin bütçe süreciyle birlikte Meclis gündemine taşınması planlanıyor. Ancak emekli maaşlarına yapılacak olası ek zam oranı ve yeni maaş tutarlarına ilişkin henüz kesin bir rakam açıklanmadı. Gabar'da iki yeni sahadan petrol haberi Erdoğan, Türkiye'nin enerji arz güvenliği ve yerli kaynakların üretime kazandırılması konusunda atılan adımlara da değindi. Karadeniz'de üretilen doğal gazla 4 milyon hanenin ihtiyacının karşılandığını belirten Erdoğan, Osmangazi Gemisi'nin devreye alınmasıyla bu sayının 8 milyona çıkarılmasının hedeflendiğini söyledi. Gabar'daki petrol üretimine ilişkin de açıklamalarda bulunan Erdoğan, bölgede iki yeni sahadan daha olumlu haber geldiğini duyurdu. Gabar'da 75,4 milyon varil Türkiye'nin en kaliteli petrolünün üretildiğini ifade etti. Türkiye'nin enerji sepetini genişletmeye, yerli petrol ve doğal gaz kaynaklarını ekonomiye kazandırmaya yönelik çalışmaların sürdüğünü vurguladı.

items.titleTr: France accuses Iran of supermarket fridge hacking
items.summaryTr: The cyber-attack last month saw fridges and freezers in hundreds of supermarkets across France heated up.
items.articleText: France accuses Iran of supermarket fridge hacking - Published France has accused Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) of being behind cyber-attacks that raised the temperatures of supermarket fridges and freezers across the country last month. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said the attack was "unprecedented in both its scale and its level of aggression", adding those who were responsible would be hit with sanctions "at the European level". Iran is yet to respond to Barrot's allegations. The cyber-attack last month saw fridges and freezers in hundreds of supermarkets across France heated up, which spoilt fresh and frozen food estimated to be worth millions of euros. Then last week, dozens of supermarkets across several other European countries were also impacted by a cyber-attack that targeted fridges and freezers. It is not known if the instances are linked. Barrot said the attack on France's supermarkets "marks the first large-scale cyber-attack aimed at sabotage on our national territory, and it constitutes a major attack on the nation's interests and the security of the French people". He said the government had summoned the Iranian ambassador to Paris to "lodge a very strong protest against this extremely grave act". France will take "any other necessary and proportionate measures" to respond to the incident and "deter anyone who might seek to repeat it", Barrot added. Separately on Monday, the Paris prosecutor said an investigation had been opened into the head of an offensive cyber unit associated with Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as well as his two deputies. Laure Beccuau named the unit as Shahid Kaveh, which she said had an affiliation with the electronic and cyber centre of the IRGC. Shahid Kaveh is the name given to a cluster of hackers thought to be directly employed by the Iranian regime. On 11 October, hackers gained control of the software that regulates the temperatures of the refrigeration units used in many of France's supermarkets. More than 100 of Coopérative U's supermarkets were hit, as well as 180 stores from Intermarché and its Netto brand. In some stores, temperatures of the fridges reportedly rose to 50C (120F) overnight. Other major food retailers including Carrefour, Monoprix and E.Leclerc were also hit by the attack, which targeted software provided by Danish engineering firm Danfoss. The software allows retailers to manage their cold units remotely. Earlier this month a second wave of hacks took place, hitting more than 100 stores across Europe. Supermarkets in Belgium and Luxembourg were affected, while a smaller number of shops were hit in countries including Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia and Finland. Separately in August a small number of US military bases had fridges mysteriously malfunction, spoiling food. This incident is also being investigated as deliberate cyber-attacks, Reuters news agency has reported, citing sources familiar with the matter. Since the waves of attacks on freezers, experts have been speculating which hacking groups could be responsible, with Iran being on a list of potential suspects. In spite of a pair of Russian-aligned hacktivist groups claiming they were responsible on Wednesday, few believed them. The French government has not said how it reached the conclusion that Iran was responsible, and attribution of cyber attacks is extremely hard as hackers are able to hide their locations. items.title: Poundland unable to buy new stock as fears over collapse grow
items.summary: The discount chain is continuing to edge towards collapse and is said to be "running on fumes", according to one insider.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Poundland unable to buy new stock as fears over collapse grow
items.summaryTr: The discount chain is continuing to edge towards collapse and is said to be "running on fumes", according to one insider.
items.articleText: Poundland unable to buy new stock as fears over collapse grow - Published Poundland is unable to buy new stock to fill its shelves after being blocked by its owners from accessing cash in its bank accounts. The discount chain is on the brink of collapse with one insider describing it as "running on fumes". It has until Thursday to secure a rescue deal. About £50m has been frozen by its American owner Gordon Brothers, the BBC understands, meaning its 600 shops are running out of stock. Pressure is building on Gordon Brothers, which bought Poundland for £1 last June, after the owner rejected a takeover bid that could have saved the thousands of jobs currently at risk. Gordon Brothers has been approached for comment. Poundland has filed a notice of intention to appoint administrators, which protects it from its creditors until Thursday. Access to funds was limited because of a tension between Gordon Brothers' dual role as both creditor and shareholder, a source said, but added they expected a relaxation of funds in the next two days. Last week, Poundland boss Barry Williams told staff like-for-like sales, which exclude new store openings, were up 11.4% last week, which included Halloween, but said this was £1.5m ahead of budget. He said the business made a profit of £18.1m in the year to September, which was a "strong recovery" from the previous year where the business made losses of £68m. The latest annual accounts have yet to be audited. - Burnham 'ready to support' Poundland staff as retailer faces collapse - Published29 October - Poundland staff protest after chain approach administrators - Published29 October However, Gordon Brothers has painted a different picture of the business, saying the chain remains "challenged and vulnerable to any potential downturn in future trading". It said it had provided significant funding to support the company's ability to trade since it acquired the business. It has also made £18m, from a combination of debt interest payments and other fees and charges. On Wednesday, executives from Gordon Brothers will appear before the Business Select Committee with MPs probing whether they are genuinely pursuing a solvent rescue of the business, which has 11,000 employees, and whether every realistic step is being taken to protect jobs and stores. The session is being held in private given commercially sensitive discussions are still under way with bidders. Uncertain future On Thursday, the 10-day moratorium to protect Poundland from its creditors expires, but if there is a prospect of a solvent deal, the deadline could be extended. If not, Poundland is set to collapse into administration and could be broken up. A source familiar with the sales process said London-based Xyra Group was making "significant progress" in its last minute bid to buy Poundland and could now be the front runner. An extension of Thursday's deadline now seems an increasingly likely scenario. But such a case would be difficult to put forward if Gordon Brothers continues to block funding. One observer remarked "if Gordon Brothers is going in front of that committee, you don't want to be giving the message we're pulling up the drawbridge". Even if a deal is agreed to sell the business as a whole, there is no guarantee a new owner would not reduce the number of stores, but suppliers to Poundland would prefer that outcome to hundreds of sites being sold off to other retailers. There has been interest from the likes of Poundstretcher, Tesco and B&M in picking up stores which could mean continuing employment for many workers. The central issue is whether a piecemeal sale would protect more jobs than a buyer willing to keep Poundland trading as a national chain.

items.title: Apple'dan Türkiye'ye 7 yeni merkez yatırımı! İlk açılış 2027'de
items.summary: Apple, Türkiye'de beş ücretsiz geliştirici akademisi, İstanbul'da bir Developer Center ve Ankara'da bir üretim akademisi açacak. İlk merkezlerin 2027'de faaliyete geçmesi planlanıyor.

items.titleTr: Apple'dan Türkiye'ye 7 yeni merkez yatırımı! İlk açılış 2027'de
items.summaryTr: Apple, Türkiye'de beş ücretsiz geliştirici akademisi, İstanbul'da bir Developer Center ve Ankara'da bir üretim akademisi açacak. İlk merkezlerin 2027'de faaliyete geçmesi planlanıyor.
items.articleText: Apple'dan Türkiye'ye 7 yeni merkez yatırımı! İlk açılış 2027'de - Apple, Türkiye'de beş ücretsiz geliştirici akademisi, İstanbul'da bir Developer Center ve Ankara'da bir üretim akademisi açacak. İlk merkezlerin 2027'de faaliyete geçmesi planlanıyor. Teknoloji devi Apple, Türkiye'deki faaliyetlerini genişletmek amacıyla yedi yeni eğitim ve teknoloji merkezi kuracağını duyurdu. 9 Kasım'da açıklanan yatırım planı kapsamında Türkiye genelinde beş Apple Developer Academy, İstanbul'da bir Apple Developer Center ve Ankara'da bir Apple Manufacturing Academy açılacak. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Yazılım geliştirme, girişimcilik ve ileri üretim teknolojilerine odaklanacak merkezlerle Türkiye'deki yazılım geliştiricilerin desteklenmesi ve küçük ve orta ölçekli işletmelerin yapay zeka destekli üretim teknolojilerine erişiminin artırılması hedefleniyor. Apple, yatırımın toplam maliyetini açıklamadı. Şirketin takvimine göre ilk geliştirici akademisi ve İstanbul'daki geliştirici merkezi 2027'de, Ankara'daki üretim akademisi ise 2028'de faaliyete başlayacak. Türkiye'de beş ücretsiz geliştirici akademisi açılacak Apple, önümüzdeki üç yıl içinde Türkiye'nin farklı noktalarında beş Apple Developer Academy kurmayı planlıyor. İlk akademi 2027 yılında İstanbul'da açılacak. Diğer dört merkezin hangi şehirlerde kurulacağı henüz açıklanmadı. Akademilerde öğrencilere ve girişimcilere dokuz ay süren ücretsiz ve yoğun eğitim programları sunulacak. Eğitimlerde kodlama, uygulama tasarımı, pazarlama, proje yönetimi ve yapay zeka teknolojilerine odaklanılacak. Programlarda erişilebilirlik, kullanıcı gizliliği ve sürdürülebilirlik konuları da ele alınacak. Apple, akademilerden önümüzdeki yıllarda binlerce öğrencinin yararlanabileceğini belirtiyor. Ancak başvuru tarihleri, kabul koşulları ve kontenjanlar henüz duyurulmadı. İstanbul, Apple'ın geliştirici merkezleri arasına katılacak Apple, 2027 yılında İstanbul'da bir Apple Developer Center da açacak. Merkez, profesyonel yazılım geliştiricilere ve teknoloji girişimlerine yönelik hizmet verecek. Geliştiriciler burada Apple uzmanlarıyla birlikte çalışma, yeni teknolojileri deneyimleme ve uygulamalarını geliştirme imkanı bulacak. Yüz yüze eğitimler, teknik atölyeler, bire bir uzman görüşmeleri ve geliştirici etkinlikleri düzenlenecek. İstanbul'daki merkez, Apple'ın Bengaluru, Berlin, Cupertino, Şanghay ve Singapur'da bulunan geliştirici merkezleri ağına katılacak. Ankara'da yapay zeka ve robotik akademisi kurulacak Yatırım planının üretim teknolojilerine yönelik ayağı ise Ankara'da hayata geçirilecek. 2028 yılında açılması planlanan Apple Manufacturing Academy, Apple'ın ABD dışındaki ilk üretim akademisi olacak. Merkezde özellikle küçük ve orta ölçekli işletmelere yönelik ücretsiz eğitimler verilecek. Programların odağında yapay zeka, makine öğrenmesi, gelişmiş otomasyon, robotik sistemler ve tahmine dayalı bakım teknolojileri bulunacak. Akademide uygulamalı eğitim laboratuvarları, teknoloji gösterimleri, ortak çalışma alanları ve profesyonel gelişim etkinlikleri de yer alacak. Ankara'daki tesisin bir üretim fabrikası olmayacağının altını çizmek gerekiyor. Merkez, Apple cihazlarının üretileceği bir tesis değil; Türkiye'deki işletmelerin ileri üretim teknolojileri konusunda eğitim ve destek alabileceği bir akademi olarak tasarlandı. Tim Cook: Türkiye'deki girişimcileri destekleyeceğiz Apple Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Tim Cook, Türkiye'deki yatırım planına ilişkin açıklamasında şirketin 35 yıldır Türkiye'deki müşterilerine ve topluluklara hizmet verdiğini hatırlattı. Türkiye'deki yazılım geliştiricilerin dünya genelinde kullanılan uygulamalar ürettiğine dikkat çeken Cook, küçük ve orta ölçekli işletmelerin de ülke ekonomisinde önemli fırsatlar yarattığını belirtti. Cook, yeni merkezlerle geliştiricilere ve işletmelere eğitim, teknoloji kaynakları ve Apple uzmanlarına doğrudan erişim sağlamayı hedeflediklerini ifade etti. Apple'ın açıkladığı plan, Türkiye'de yazılım geliştirme ve ileri üretim teknolojileri alanlarında yeni eğitim imkanları oluşturmayı amaçlıyor. Ancak yatırımın toplam finansal büyüklüğü, yaratacağı istihdam ve merkezlerin kesin öğrenci kapasiteleri henüz açıklanmış değil.

items.articleText: BİM'in (BIMAS) kârı yüzde 79 arttı! Üçüncü çeyrekte 10,4 milyar TL net kâr - BİM, 2026'nın ilk 9 ayında 26,15 milyar TL net kâr açıkladı. Şirketin net kârı yıllık bazda yüzde 79 artarken, üçüncü çeyrek kârı 10,39 milyar TL ile piyasa beklentilerini aştı. BİM Birleşik Mağazalar A.Ş. (BIMAS), 2026 yılı üçüncü çeyrek finansal sonuçlarını 9 Kasım'da Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu'nda (KAP) yayımladı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Şirket, 1 Ocak-30 Eylül 2026 döneminde 26 milyar 151 milyon 834 bin TL net dönem kârı elde etti. BİM, 2025'in aynı döneminde 14 milyar 598 milyon 567 bin TL net kâr açıklamıştı. Böylece şirketin 9 aylık net kârı yıllık bazda yüzde 79 arttı. items.titleTr: Analysts see no broader ‘contagion’ from $6.3B Binance hack
items.summaryTr: Binance’s pledge to cover all user losses helped contain the fallout from the $6.3 billion hack, analysts said.
items.articleText: Analysts see no broader ‘contagion’ from $6.3B Binance hack Binance’s pledge to cover all user losses helped contain the fallout from the $6.3 billion hack, analysts said. Binance’s pledge to cover user losses from its $6.3 billion hack helped contain the fallout across crypto markets, analysts told Cointelegraph. “There doesn’t seem to be any contagion-type effect from the hack, given that Binance is able to cover the losses using its balance sheet,” Martin Lee, market insights lead at DWF Labs, told Cointelegraph. He said investors turned their focus to the implications of the US midterm elections. Binance’s daily net outflows fell to $458 million in the 24 hours leading to Monday’s publication time, down from $6.1 billion on Nov. 2 after withdrawals resumed, according to DefiLlama. Attackers stole about $6.3 billion from Binance hot wallets in the Oct. 29 breach, making it the largest crypto hack to date. Bitcoin (BTC) fell as much as 5.7% over the first five days after the hack, a decline CryptoQuant called “modest” in its Wednesday report . Bitcoin fell roughly 13.6% after the $1.4 billion Bybit hack in 2025 and about 9.9% after the Coincheck hack in 2018. At least 14 of the past 38 hacks CryptoQuant reviewed were followed by steeper Bitcoin declines. Bitcoin’s drawdown after the Binance hack, compared to previous exchange hacks. Source: CryptoQuant Major exchange hacks have previously triggered “short-lived drawdowns that markets later absorbed” as long-term holder demand returned, Lacie Zhang, research lead at Bitget Wallet, told Cointelegraph, adding that the Binance hack does not represent a “structural trend reversal” for crypto markets. Related: Binance hackers had 8-week intrusion window before $6.3B exploit: SEAL Bitfinex analysts say CPI could help confirm a Bitcoin bottom “Much of the hack’s impact now looks priced in,” with Bitcoin currently trading at an “attractive level,” Bitfinex analysts told Cointelegraph. “Confirmation of a market bottom now depends on the Consumer Price Index (CPI) reading due on 10 November, which will shape the Federal Reserve’s next rate decision. Higher bond yields would put pressure on risk assets.” Market participants priced in an 80% chance that the Federal Reserve will raise rates at its Dec. 9 meeting, up from 69% a month earlier, according to the CMEGroup’s FedWatch tool. Bitcoin fell 2.5% over 24 hours to $74,580 as of 1:21 pm UTC on Monday, according to CoinMarketCap. Magazine: Vitalik ‘pivots’ ETH to store of value, crypto suffers after US midterms: Hodler’s Digest

items.summaryTr: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
items.articleText: Here’s what happened in crypto today Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation. Today in crypto, the European Union called on the finance industry to write a common rulebook for tokenized securities, Zcash developers seek another reduction in block times and Binance France is closing up shop in the country. EU taps industry to set standards for tokenized securities The European Central Bank, European Commission and European Securities and Markets Authority are seeking nominations for an industry-led group that will draft common standards for holding and settling tokenized securities. Eligible applicants include EU industry associations, global institutions, private firms and fintech companies. They can apply to the European Tokenisation Standards Group (ETSG) by Nov. 27, with work set to begin in January 2027, according to a release published Monday. The three EU institutions will participate as observers. The group will develop technical and market standards to help companies hold and settle tokenized securities across different distributed ledger technology (DLT) platforms and ensure those platforms can work with existing financial systems. The group aims to produce an initial set of standards by early 2028, according to its mandate. The standards will support Appia, the Eurosystem’s initiative to develop a blueprint for Europe’s tokenized financial markets. The institutions warned that fragmentation could limit the benefits of tokenization and said the group may recommend ways for EU authorities to encourage firms to adopt its standards. In September, the Eurosystem launched Pontes, a system that allows financial institutions to settle wholesale transactions in tokenized assets in central bank money. Zcash devs propose another block time cut days after NU7 upgrade Zcash developers have proposed reducing the blockchain’s target block interval from 25 seconds to 20 seconds, seeking faster transaction confirmations days after activating the NU7 upgrade. On Sunday, developers ValarDragon and Evan Forbes submitted a draft Zcash Improvement Proposal (ZIP) on GitHub, saying that they want the change to be included in the next community poll and considered for the upcoming NU7.1 network upgrade. The reduction would shorten the expected wait for initial transaction confirmations. According to the proposal, this would improve the user experience for point-of-sale payments, exchange deposits and cross-chain swaps. The developers said the change would not increase the network’s overall daily capacity for private transactions. The proposal would also preserve Zcash’s existing issuance schedule, despite blocks being produced more frequently. The proposal comes just days after Zcash’s NU7 upgrade went live. On Friday, the NU7 upgrade was activated on the mainnet, cutting the network’s target block interval from 75 seconds to 25 seconds. The upgrade also introduced a Network Sustainability Mechanism designed to recycle a portion of transaction fees into future mining rewards while preserving Zcash’s 21 million ZEC supply cap. Binance France emails announce closure of accounts Dec. 31 Binance France is closing up shop in the country. Customers have been notified by email during early November, according to media reports. All accounts will be closed on Dec. 31, and any assets left on the exchange will be charged monthly fees starting on Nov. 29, Cryptoast, Crypto Briefing and other media reported on Saturday, citing emails sent to users by Binance. On that date, accounts still maintaining a balance will pay a monthly maintenance fee of 0.025% of the balance, or a minimum of 10 USDC, a stablecoin tracking the US dollar. To avoid fees, withdrawals must be completed by Nov. 29, the exchange said.

items.title: The $2.85B Binance hackers lost shows why the UK needs stablecoin freeze rules
items.summary: The Binance hack proved stablecoin freezes work. Now the UK should make clear freeze rules a condition of listing coins.

items.titleTr: The $2.85B Binance hackers lost shows why the UK needs stablecoin freeze rules
items.summaryTr: The Binance hack proved stablecoin freezes work. Now the UK should make clear freeze rules a condition of listing coins.
items.articleText: The $2.85B Binance hackers lost shows why the UK needs stablecoin freeze rules The Binance hack proved stablecoin freezes work. Now the UK should make clear freeze rules a condition of listing coins. Opinion by Lissele Pratt, co-founder, Capitalixe Last weekend, the Federal Bureau of Investigation claimed that North Korea was behind the $6.3 billion Binance hack, which analysts are calling the largest heist on record. While I’ve read a lot about the scale of this heist, far less has been said about what went right. Because while it is true that the perpetrators stole $6.3 billion, they haven’t actually been able to hold on to a significant proportion of those takings. $2.85 billion of the funds has been frozen. The reason for this comes down to what the stolen money was comprised of. Of that $2.85 billion, 94% was held in stablecoins. While this hack was terrible news all around, it did show that centralized control, oftentimes criticized by crypto purists, might actually be one of the strongest tools we have against crypto crime. Because, unlike other assets, stablecoins can be frozen by their issuers, giving victims a real chance to stop stolen money reaching the wrong hands. It does, however, raise an uncomfortable question. If private companies have the power to freeze billions of dollars in assets, who decides when they should be allowed to use it? The United Kingdom now has the opportunity to do just that. The race to get rid of stablecoins To get an idea of just how much the freeze mattered, you just have to look at what the hackers did within the first hour of their heist. Related: Binance, Polymarket seek Polygon hard fork to recover $6.8M in stolen crypto Clearly, they understood that there was a very limited window to move the stablecoins before anyone could stop them. So that’s exactly what they did. What was frozen from the Binance hack. Source: Elliptic Less than an hour after the hack began, they had already sold $325 million worth of stolen USDT (Tether’s stablecoin) for Ether. The reasoning behind this was to swap an asset that could be frozen with one that could not. Luckily, stablecoin issuers were quick to act, with Tether’s first major freeze coming just 37 minutes after the stolen funds reached the hackers’ main wallet, and Circle following three minutes later, blocking the movement of USDC. Without Tether and Circle intervening, far more of the funds could have ended up beyond their reach. We’re yet to agree on the rules The freeze, to its credit, worked for the most part because a handful of companies decided, in real time, to use it. The problem is that there still isn’t an agreed standard that outlines when a freeze is justified or how quickly the response needs to be, and we’re beginning to see the consequences of not having these answers. For instance, Circle is facing a proposed class action from Drift Protocol investors who allege it failed to freeze around $230 million in stolen USDC after the April hack. Their argument is that Circle could have stopped the money from moving, but didn’t act in time. Meanwhile, Tether is being sued in New York by two businessmen who claim it froze millions of their assets months before a seizure warrant existed. It’s important to mention that Tether has responded to this case, calling these allegations baseless. Working in payments and banking, it’s not uncommon for me to see traditional banks freeze money and accounts. Due to this, you may argue that if a bank can do this frequently, why shouldn’t a stablecoin issuer be able to? Stablecoin freeze timeline. Source: CertiK My argument isn’t that they shouldn’t. But banks don’t get to decide they want to freeze assets out of nowhere. There’s usually a legal trigger behind their decision, as well as a way to challenge it. Stablecoin issuers now hold the same power while having to act faster and across borders. So it’s about time they’re given some structure. Britain can fix this There is, however, a caveat with regulating stablecoin issuers. Tether and Circle, two of the largest issuers, aren’t based in the UK, so British regulators can’t simply tell them what to do. Related: Binance traces $6.3B hack to fake job interviews, compromised AI tool What Britain can control, though, is which stablecoins UK customers are allowed to buy, and they’ve already begun doing so. In June, the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) published its cryptoassets regime. Under it, UK trading platforms must carry out due diligence and publish a disclosure document before they list a coin, and that includes stablecoins issued overseas. It comes into force on 25 October 2027. The Bank of England is finalizing its Code of Practice for systemic stablecoin issuers by the end of this year. It covers stablecoins used widely enough for payments to matter to UK financial stability. Neither framework establishes the clear obligations around freezing stolen funds that I believe are necessary. But both are still taking shape, giving the UK the perfect opportunity to address this gap now, rather than trying to retrofit new requirements later. Two conditions for a UK listing So here’s a solution that I believe would work. Before a stablecoin can be sold on a UK platform, its issuer should have to agree to two conditions. The first being that it is contactable and ready to act. Tether and Circle did exactly that last week, but the victim was the world’s biggest exchange. A small UK platform should get the same response. I work with a number of smaller crypto businesses that don’t have Binance’s profile or a direct line to Tether. Under the current system, they’re the ones most likely to be left waiting. The second is that there needs to be a clear timetable for what happens next. If an issuer freezes funds, it should notify the National Crime Agency that same day. The freeze should then expire if there hasn’t been a court order put out to keep the wallet frozen. Neither of these are extremely controversial takes. They’d give law enforcement a chance to intervene when money is stolen and also protect people from having their assets frozen indefinitely, without legal grounds. The Binance hack has shown us that stablecoins can give victims of crypto crime a chance to stop stolen money before it’s gone for good. That shouldn’t be a privilege reserved only for the world’s biggest exchanges. Magazine: Can decentralized phone networks power the AI revolution?
